sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第105卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 105
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 105

sentences.zh: 卷第一百五

translations.literal: Volume 105
translations.idiomatic: Volume One Hundred and Five

sentences.zh: 【晉紀二十七】　起昭陽協洽，盡閼逢涒灘，凡二年。

translations.literal: [Jin Records 27] Beginning in Zhaoyang Xiehe and ending in Efeng Tuntan—in all, two years.
translations.idiomatic: [Jin Records 27] From the year Zhaoyang Xiehe through Efeng Tuntan, spanning two years in all.

sentences.zh: 烈宗孝武皇帝上之下太元八年（

translations.literal: Lie Zong, Emperor Xiaowu, First Part, Lower Section, Year 8 of Taiyuan (
translations.idiomatic: Lie Zong, Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, Part One, Lower Section, Eighth Year of the Taiyuan reign (

sentences.zh: 癸未，公元三八三年）

translations.literal: Guiwei, A.D. 383)
translations.idiomatic: the year Guiwei, equivalent to A.D. 383)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，秦呂光發長安，以鄯善王休密馱、車師前部王彌窴為鄉導。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Lü Guang of Qin set out from Chang'an, taking King Xiumituo of Shanshan and King Mizhi of the Front Division of Cheshi as guides.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, during the first month, Lü Guang of Former Qin marched out from Chang'an, with the Shanshan king Xiumituo and Mizhi, king of the Front Division of Cheshi, serving as his guides.

sentences.zh: 三月，丁巳，大赦。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day Dingsi, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day Dingsi, the court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，桓沖帥眾十萬伐秦，攻襄陽；

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, Huan Chong led a force of one hundred thousand to attack Qin and assault Xiangyang;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, during the fifth month, Huan Chong led one hundred thousand men in a campaign against Qin and laid siege to Xiangyang;

sentences.zh: 遣前將軍劉波等攻沔北諸城；

translations.literal: he sent Forward General Liu Bo and others to attack the cities north of the Mian River;
translations.idiomatic: he dispatched Forward General Liu Bo and others to strike the cities north of the Mian;

sentences.zh: 輔國將軍楊亮攻蜀，拔五城，進攻涪城；

translations.literal: Auxiliary State General Yang Liang attacked Shu, captured five cities, and advanced to attack Fucheng;
translations.idiomatic: Auxiliary State General Yang Liang invaded Shu, took five cities, and pressed on against Fucheng;

sentences.zh: 鷹揚將軍郭銓攻武當。

translations.literal: Soaring Hawk General Guo Quan attacked Wudang.
translations.idiomatic: Soaring Hawk General Guo Quan attacked Wudang.

sentences.zh: 六月，沖別將攻萬歲、築陽，拔之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, one of Chong's detached generals attacked Wansui and Zhuyang and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, one of Chong's detached commanders attacked Wansui and Zhuyang and took both.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅遣征南將軍巨鹿公睿、冠軍將軍慕容垂等帥步騎五萬救襄陽，兗州刺史張崇救武當，後將軍張蚝、步兵校尉姚萇救涪城；

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin sent Campaign-South General the Duke of Julu, Fu Rui, Champion General Murong Chui, and others to lead fifty thousand infantry and cavalry to relieve Xiangyang; Yanzhou Inspector Zhang Chong relieved Wudang; Rear General Zhang Hao and Foot-Soldier Commandant Yao Chang relieved Fucheng;
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian of Qin sent Campaign-South General the Duke of Julu, Fu Rui, Champion General Murong Chui, and others at the head of fifty thousand foot and horse to relieve Xiangyang; Yanzhou inspector Zhang Chong went to the aid of Wudang; rear general Zhang Hao and foot-soldier commandant Yao Chang marched to relieve Fucheng;

sentences.zh: 睿軍於新野，垂軍於鄧城。

translations.literal: Rui encamped at Xinye, and Chui at Dengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Rui encamped at Xinye while Chui took position at Dengcheng.

sentences.zh: 桓沖退屯沔南。

translations.literal: Huan Chong withdrew and encamped south of the Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Chong pulled back and encamped south of the Mian River.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，郭銓及冠軍將軍桓石虔敗張崇於武當，掠二千戶以歸。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Guo Quan and Champion General Huan Shiqian defeated Zhang Chong at Wudang and carried off two thousand households on their return.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, during the seventh month, Guo Quan and Champion General Huan Shiqian defeated Zhang Chong at Wudang and drove off two thousand households on their way back.

sentences.zh: 巨鹿公睿遣慕容垂為前鋒，進臨沔水。

translations.literal: The Duke of Julu, Fu Rui, sent Murong Chui as vanguard and advanced to the Mian River.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Julu, Fu Rui, sent Murong Chui forward as vanguard to the banks of the Mian.

sentences.zh: 垂夜命軍士人持十炬，繫於樹枝，光照數十里。

translations.literal: At night Chui ordered each soldier to hold ten torches tied to tree branches, and the light shone for several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: That night Chui had every soldier take ten torches and tie them to the branches of trees, and the glare stretched for dozens of li.

sentences.zh: 沖懼，退還上明。

translations.literal: Chong was afraid and withdrew to Shangming.
translations.idiomatic: Chong took fright and fell back to Shangming.

sentences.zh: 張蚝出斜谷，楊亮引兵還。

translations.literal: Zhang Hao came out through Xiegu, and Yang Liang led his troops back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hao marched out through Xiegu, and Yang Liang withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 沖表其兄子石民領襄城太守，戍夏口，沖自求領江州刺史；

translations.literal: Chong memorialized that his elder brother's son Shimin should be made Administrator of Xiangcheng and garrison Xiakou, while he himself requested to take charge as Inspector of Jiangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Chong submitted a memorial asking that his elder brother's son Shimin be appointed administrator of Xiangcheng to garrison Xiakou, while he himself sought appointment as inspector of Jiangzhou;

sentences.zh: 詔許之。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved his request.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅下詔大舉入寇，民每十丁遣一兵；

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin issued an edict for a great invasion: for every ten male subjects, one soldier was to be levied;
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian of Qin issued an edict ordering a massive invasion, conscripting one soldier from every ten male subjects;

sentences.zh: 其良家子年二十已下，有材勇者，皆拜羽林郎。

translations.literal: among the sons of good families under twenty years of age who were talented and brave, all were appointed Feathered Forest Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: and every able-bodied youth under twenty from a respectable family was commissioned as a Feathered Forest gentleman.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「其以司馬昌明為尚書左僕射，謝安為吏部尚書，桓沖為侍中；

translations.literal: It also said: "Let Sima Changming be made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Xie An Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and Huan Chong Palace Attendant;
translations.idiomatic: The edict also read: "Let Sima Changming be appointed left vice director of the Masters of Writing, Xie An minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and Huan Chong palace attendant;

sentences.zh: 勢還不遠，可先為起第。」

translations.literal: their return is not far off—mansions may first be built for them."
translations.idiomatic: they will not be long in returning—you may begin building mansions for them in advance."

sentences.zh: 良家子至者三萬餘騎，拜秦州主簿，金城趙盛之為少年都統。

translations.literal: More than thirty thousand cavalry of good-family youths arrived; Zhao Shengzhi of Jincheng was made Chief Clerk of Qinzhou and commander-in-chief of the youths.
translations.idiomatic: More than thirty thousand mounted youths from good families arrived; Zhao Shengzhi of Jincheng was appointed chief clerk of Qinzhou and commander-in-chief of the young recruits.

sentences.zh: 是時，朝臣皆不欲堅行，獨慕容垂、姚萇及良家子勸之。

translations.literal: At this time all the court ministers did not wish Fu Jian to go on campaign; only Murong Chui, Yao Chang, and the good-family youths urged him.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the court ministers were united in opposing the campaign; only Murong Chui, Yao Chang, and the young recruits from good families urged Fu Jian on.

sentences.zh: 陽平公融言於堅曰：「鮮卑、羌虜，我之仇讎，常思風塵之變以逞其志，所陳策畫，何可從也！

translations.literal: Duke of Yangping, Fu Rong, said to Fu Jian: "The Xianbei and Qiang barbarians are our mortal enemies; they constantly look for turmoil in which to fulfill their ambitions—how can their proposed plans be followed!
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Yangping, Fu Rong, said to Fu Jian: "The Xianbei and Qiang are our mortal foes; they are always watching for turmoil in which to realize their ambitions. How can we heed the plans they propose!

sentences.zh: 良家少年皆富饒子弟，不閒軍旅，苟為諂諛之言以會陛下之意耳。

translations.literal: These good-family youths are all sons of wealthy houses, unversed in military affairs, who merely offer flattering words to suit Your Majesty's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: These youths from good families are all sons of wealthy houses with no experience of war; they offer nothing but flattery tailored to Your Majesty's wishes.

sentences.zh: 今陛下信而用之，輕舉大事，臣恐功既不成，仍有後患，悔無及也！」

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty trusts and employs them and lightly undertakes this great affair—I fear that even if success is not achieved, there will still be later troubles, and regret will come too late!"
translations.idiomatic: Now that Your Majesty trusts and follows them in lightly undertaking this great campaign, I fear that even if it fails, worse troubles will follow—and then regret will come too late!"

sentences.zh: 堅不聽。

translations.literal: Fu Jian would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 八月，戊午，堅遣陽平公融督張蚝、慕容垂等步騎二十五萬為前鋒；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day Wuwu, Fu Jian sent the Duke of Yangping, Fu Rong, to supervise Zhang Hao, Murong Chui, and others with two hundred fifty thousand infantry and cavalry as the vanguard;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the day Wuwu, Fu Jian dispatched the Duke of Yangping, Fu Rong, to command Zhang Hao, Murong Chui, and others at the head of two hundred fifty thousand foot and horse as the vanguard;

sentences.zh: 以兗州刺史姚萇為龍驤將軍，督益、梁州諸軍事。

translations.literal: he made Yanzhou Inspector Yao Chang Dragon-soaring General and supervisor of military affairs in Yi and Liang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: and he appointed Yanzhou inspector Yao Chang Dragon-Soaring General with overall command of military affairs in Yi and Liang.

sentences.zh: 堅謂萇曰：「昔朕以龍驤建業，未嘗輕以授人，卿其勉之！」

translations.literal: Fu Jian said to Chang: "Formerly I founded my enterprise as Dragon-soaring General and have never lightly bestowed that title on anyone—you must exert yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian told Chang: "Long ago I founded my realm as Dragon-Soaring General and have never lightly bestowed that title on anyone. You must prove yourself worthy of it!"

sentences.zh: 左將軍竇沖曰：「王者無戲言，此不祥之征也！」

translations.literal: Left General Dou Chong said: "A king does not speak in jest—this is an ill-omened sign!"
translations.idiomatic: Left General Dou Chong said: "A king does not speak in jest—this is an ill omen!"

sentences.zh: 堅默然。

translations.literal: Fu Jian fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian said nothing.

sentences.zh: 慕容楷、慕容紹言於慕容垂曰：「主上驕矜已甚，叔父建中興之業，在此行也！」

translations.literal: Murong Kai and Murong Shao said to Murong Chui: "Our lord's arrogance has already gone too far—Uncle, the enterprise of restoring our house rests on this campaign!"
translations.idiomatic: Murong Kai and Murong Shao said to Murong Chui: "Our lord has grown unbearably arrogant. Uncle, the work of restoring our house rests on this campaign!"

sentences.zh: 垂曰：「然。

translations.literal: Chui said: "So it is.
translations.idiomatic: Chui said: "Indeed.

sentences.zh: 非汝，誰與成之！」

translations.literal: Without you, with whom could it be accomplished!"
translations.idiomatic: Without you, who else could bring it about!"

sentences.zh: 甲子，堅發長安，戎卒六十餘萬，騎二十七萬，旗鼓相望，前後千里。

translations.literal: On the day Jiazi, Fu Jian set out from Chang'an with more than six hundred thousand foot soldiers and two hundred seventy thousand cavalry; banners and drums faced one another for a thousand li front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiazi, Fu Jian marched out from Chang'an at the head of more than six hundred thousand foot soldiers and two hundred seventy thousand horsemen, with banners and drums stretching in an unbroken line for a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 九月，堅至項城，涼州之兵始達咸陽，蜀、漢之兵方順流而下，幽、冀之兵至於彭城，東西萬里，水陸齊進，運漕萬艘。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Fu Jian reached Xiangcheng; troops from Liangzhou had only just reached Xianyang, those from Shu and Han were still coming downstream, and those from You and Ji had reached Pengcheng—ten thousand li east and west, advancing together by land and water, with ten thousand grain transports.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Fu Jian reached Xiangcheng while Liangzhou troops were only just arriving at Xianyang, Shu and Han forces were still coming downstream, and You and Ji troops had reached Pengcheng—armies spread ten thousand li east and west, advancing together by land and water behind ten thousand grain transports.

sentences.zh: 陽平公融等兵三十萬，先至穎口。

translations.literal: The Duke of Yangping, Fu Rong, and others with three hundred thousand troops arrived first at Yingkou.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Yangping, Fu Rong, and his three hundred thousand men reached Yingkou ahead of the main body.

sentences.zh: 詔以尚書僕射謝石為征虜將軍、征討大都督，以徐、兗二州刺史謝玄為前鋒都督，與輔國將軍謝琰、西中郎將桓伊等眾共八萬拒之；

translations.literal: An edict appointed Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xie Shi as General Who Subdues Barbarians and Grand Commander for the punitive campaign, and Xu and Yanzhou Inspector Xie Xuan as Vanguard Commander; with Auxiliary State General Xie Yan, Western Central Commander Huan Yi, and others, a total of eighty thousand troops were to resist;
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xie Shi general who subdues barbarians and grand commander of the punitive campaign, with Xu and Yanzhou inspector Xie Xuan as vanguard commander; together with Auxiliary State General Xie Yan, Western Central Commander Huan Yi, and others, they fielded eighty thousand men to meet the invasion;

sentences.zh: 使龍驤將軍胡彬以水軍五千援壽陽。

translations.literal: Dragon-soaring General Hu Bin was sent with five thousand naval troops to reinforce Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon-Soaring General Hu Bin was dispatched with five thousand sailors to reinforce Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 琰，安之子也。

translations.literal: Yan was the son of Xie An.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was Xie An's son.

sentences.zh: 是時，秦兵既盛，都下震恐。

translations.literal: At this time the Qin forces were already powerful, and the capital was shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Qin armies had grown overwhelming, and panic spread through the capital.

sentences.zh: 謝玄入，問計於謝安，安夷然，答曰：「已別有旨。」

translations.literal: Xie Xuan entered and asked Xie An for a plan; An remained placid and replied: "Separate instructions have already been issued."
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xuan came in to ask Xie An for counsel; An remained perfectly calm and answered: "Instructions have already been issued."

sentences.zh: 既而寂然。

translations.literal: Then he fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Then he said no more.

sentences.zh: 玄不敢復言，乃令張玄重請。

translations.literal: Xuan did not dare speak again and had Zhang Xuan press the question once more.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan dared not press further and had Zhang Xuan ask again.

sentences.zh: 安遂命駕出遊山墅，親朋畢集，與圍棋賭墅。

translations.literal: An then ordered his carriage and went out to his mountain villa; when kinsmen and friends had all gathered, he played go with them, wagering the villa.
translations.idiomatic: An then had his carriage brought and went out to his mountain villa, where he gathered kinsmen and friends and played go with them, wagering the villa itself on the outcome.

sentences.zh: 安棋常劣於玄，是日，玄懼，便為敵手而又不勝。

translations.literal: An's play was usually inferior to Xuan's; that day Xuan, in his anxiety, played as An's equal and still could not win.
translations.idiomatic: An was usually the weaker player, but that day Xuan, preoccupied with fear, played as his equal and still could not beat him.

sentences.zh: 安遂游陟，至夜乃還。

translations.literal: An then strolled about the hills and did not return until night.
translations.idiomatic: An then wandered the hills and did not return until nightfall.

sentences.zh: 桓沖深以根本為憂，遣精銳三千入援京師。

translations.literal: Huan Chong was deeply worried about the foundation of the state and sent three thousand picked troops to reinforce the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Chong, deeply worried for the dynasty's survival, sent three thousand elite troops to reinforce the capital.

sentences.zh: 謝安固卻之，曰：「朝廷處分已定，兵甲無闕，西籓宜留以為防。」

translations.literal: Xie An firmly declined them, saying: "The court's dispositions are already settled, arms are not lacking, and the western defense should be kept in place."
translations.idiomatic: Xie An firmly refused them, saying: "The court has already settled its dispositions, arms are ample, and the western defenses must be held in place."

sentences.zh: 沖對佐吏歎曰：「謝安右有廟堂之量，不閒將略。

translations.literal: Chong said to his staff with a sigh: "Xie An truly has the measure of a statesman in council, but he is unversed in military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Chong sighed to his staff: "Xie An has the breadth of mind for council chambers, but he knows nothing of military strategy.

sentences.zh: 今大敵垂至，方游談不暇，遣諸不經事少年拒之，眾又寡弱，天下事已可知，吾其左衽矣！」

translations.literal: Now with a great enemy about to arrive, he is still at leisure for excursions and talk, sending untried youths to resist, and our forces are few and weak—the outcome of the realm is already clear: I shall have to wear my coat with the left lapel!"
translations.idiomatic: With a great enemy upon us, he still has leisure for outings and conversation, and sends untried youths to hold them off with a force too small and weak—the fate of the realm is already plain. I shall soon be wearing my coat with the left lapel!"

sentences.zh: 以琅邪王道子錄尚書六條事。

translations.literal: The Prince of Langye, Sima Daozi, was put in charge of recording the six categories of Masters of Writing business.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Langye, Sima Daozi, was appointed to oversee the six categories of Masters of Writing business.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，秦陽平公融等攻壽陽；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, the Qin Duke of Yangping, Fu Rong, and others attacked Shouyang;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, during the tenth month, the Qin Duke of Yangping, Fu Rong, and his forces attacked Shouyang;

sentences.zh: 癸酉，克之，執平虜將軍徐元喜等。

translations.literal: on the day Guiyou they captured it and took Pacify-the-Barbarians General Xu Yuanxi and others prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: on the day Guiyou they took the city and captured Pacify-the-Barbarians General Xu Yuanxi and others.

sentences.zh: 融以其參軍河南郭褒為淮南太守。

translations.literal: Rong made his staff officer Guo Bao of Henan Administrator of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Rong appointed his staff officer Guo Bao of Henan administrator of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂拔鄖城。

translations.literal: Murong Chui captured Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui took Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 胡彬聞壽陽陷，退保硤石，融進攻之。

translations.literal: When Hu Bin heard that Shouyang had fallen, he withdrew to defend Xiashi; Rong advanced to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu Bin learned that Shouyang had fallen, he withdrew to hold Xiashi, and Rong pressed the attack.

sentences.zh: 秦衛將軍梁成等帥眾五萬屯於洛澗，柵淮以遏東兵。

translations.literal: Qin Guard General Liang Cheng and others led fifty thousand troops to encamp at Luojian, palisading the Huai to block the eastern armies.
translations.idiomatic: Qin guard general Liang Cheng and others led fifty thousand men to encamp at Luojian, fortifying the Huai to block the eastern armies.

sentences.zh: 謝石、謝玄等去洛澗二十五里而軍，憚成，不敢進。

translations.literal: Xie Shi, Xie Xuan, and others encamped twenty-five li from Luojian, fearing Cheng and not daring to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shi, Xie Xuan, and the others encamped twenty-five li from Luojian, afraid of Liang Cheng and unwilling to advance.

sentences.zh: 胡彬糧盡，潛遣使告石等曰：「今賊盛，糧盡，恐不復見大軍！」

translations.literal: Hu Bin's grain was exhausted; he secretly sent a messenger to tell Shi and the others: "The enemy is now strong and our grain is gone—I fear we shall not see the main army again!"
translations.idiomatic: Hu Bin's supplies ran out; he secretly sent a messenger to Shi and the others saying: "The enemy is overwhelming and our grain is gone—I fear we shall never see the main army again!"

sentences.zh: 秦人獲之，送於陽平公融。

translations.literal: The Qin forces captured him and sent him to the Duke of Yangping, Fu Rong.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin captured the messenger and sent him to the Duke of Yangping, Fu Rong.

sentences.zh: 融馳使白秦王堅曰：「賊少易擒，但恐逃去，宜速赴之！」

translations.literal: Rong hurriedly sent word to King Fu Jian: "The enemy are few and easy to capture, but I fear they may escape—you should come quickly!"
translations.idiomatic: Rong hurried a message to King Fu Jian: "The enemy are few and easily taken, but they may escape—you should come at once!"

sentences.zh: 堅乃留大軍於項城，引輕騎八千，兼道就融於壽陽。

translations.literal: Fu Jian then left the main army at Xiangcheng and led eight thousand light cavalry by forced marches to join Rong at Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian left the main army at Xiangcheng and rode hard with eight thousand light cavalry to join Rong at Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 遣尚書朱序來說謝石等以「強弱異勢，不如速降。」

translations.literal: He sent Master of Writing Zhu Xu to persuade Xie Shi and the others that "strong and weak are mismatched—better to surrender quickly."
translations.idiomatic: He sent Master of Writing Zhu Xu to tell Xie Shi and the others that "given the disparity in strength, you would do better to surrender at once."

sentences.zh: 序私謂石等曰：「若秦百萬之眾盡至，誠難與為敵。

translations.literal: Privately Xu said to Shi and the others: "If Qin's million troops all arrive, they will indeed be hard to oppose.
translations.idiomatic: Privately Xu told Shi and the others: "If Qin's full force of a million men arrives, you truly cannot stand against them.

sentences.zh: 今乘諸軍未集，宜速擊之；

translations.literal: Now, while their armies are not yet gathered, you should strike quickly;
translations.idiomatic: But while their armies are still gathering, you should strike at once;

sentences.zh: 若敗其前鋒，則彼已奪氣，可遂破也。」

translations.literal: if you defeat their vanguard, their spirit will already be broken and they can then be destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: defeat their vanguard and their spirit will break—then you can rout them completely."

sentences.zh: 石聞堅在壽陽，甚懼，欲不戰以老秦師。

translations.literal: When Shi heard that Fu Jian was at Shouyang, he was greatly afraid and wished not to fight but to wear down the Qin army.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi learned that Fu Jian was at Shouyang, he was terrified and wanted to avoid battle and wear the Qin army down.

sentences.zh: 謝琰勸石從序言。

translations.literal: Xie Yan urged Shi to follow Xu's advice.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yan urged Shi to follow Xu's counsel.

sentences.zh: 十一月，謝玄遣廣陵相劉牢之帥精兵五千人趣洛澗，未至十里，梁成阻澗為陳以待之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Xie Xuan sent the Administrator of Guangling, Liu Laozhi, with five thousand picked troops toward Luojian; before they had gone ten li, Liang Cheng blocked the stream and formed battle lines to await them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Xie Xuan sent Liu Laozhi, administrator of Guangling, at the head of five thousand elite troops toward Luojian; before they had marched ten li, Liang Cheng barred the stream and drew up in battle order to meet them.

sentences.zh: 牢之直前渡水，擊成，大破之，斬成及弋陽太守王詠，又分兵斷其歸津，秦步騎崩潰，爭赴淮水，士卒死者萬五千人。

translations.literal: Laozhi went straight forward, crossed the water, attacked Cheng, and routed him decisively, beheading Cheng and Yiyang Administrator Wang Yong; he also detached troops to cut off their line of retreat, and the Qin infantry and cavalry collapsed, rushing toward the Huai—fifteen thousand soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi pressed straight ahead, crossed the water, and smashed Liang Cheng's force, killing Cheng and Yiyang administrator Wang Yong; he also detached troops to cut off their retreat, and the Qin foot and horse collapsed in rout toward the Huai, leaving fifteen thousand dead.

sentences.zh: 執秦揚州刺史王顯等，盡收其器械軍實。

translations.literal: They captured Qin Yangzhou Inspector Wang Xian and others and took all their weapons and military stores.
translations.idiomatic: They captured Qin Yangzhou inspector Wang Xian and others and seized all their weapons and supplies.

sentences.zh: 於是謝石等諸軍水陸繼進。

translations.literal: Thereupon the armies of Xie Shi and the others advanced in succession by land and water.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the armies under Xie Shi and the others pressed forward by land and water.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅與陽平公融登壽陽城望之。

translations.literal: King Fu Jian and the Duke of Yangping, Fu Rong, ascended the wall of Shouyang to look at them.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian and the Duke of Yangping, Fu Rong, climbed the walls of Shouyang to watch them.

sentences.zh: 見晉兵部陣嚴整，又望見八公山上草木，皆以為晉兵，顧謂融曰：「此亦勁敵，何謂弱也！」

translations.literal: Seeing the Jin troops' formations strict and orderly, and looking at the grass and trees on Mount Bagong and taking them all for Jin soldiers, he turned and said to Rong: "These too are formidable foes—why call them weak!"
translations.idiomatic: He saw the Jin ranks drawn up in tight order, and when he looked at the grass and trees on Mount Bagong he took every bush for a Jin soldier; turning to Rong he said: "These are formidable enemies too—why did you call them weak!"

sentences.zh: 憮然始有懼色。

translations.literal: Distressed, he showed fear for the first time.
translations.idiomatic: His face fell, and for the first time he showed fear.

sentences.zh: 秦兵逼肥水而陳，晉兵不得渡。

translations.literal: The Qin troops drew up close to the Fei River, and the Jin troops could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin army drew up hard against the Fei River, and the Jin forces could not get across.

sentences.zh: 謝玄遣使謂陽平公融曰：「君懸軍深入，而置陳逼水，此乃持久之計，非欲速戰者也。

translations.literal: Xie Xuan sent a messenger to say to the Duke of Yangping, Fu Rong: "You have led your army deep into enemy territory and set your lines hard against the water—this is a plan for a long campaign, not for seeking a quick battle.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xuan sent a messenger to the Duke of Yangping, Fu Rong: "You have marched deep into hostile country and pitched your lines against the river—clearly you mean to fight a war of attrition, not seek a quick decision.

sentences.zh: 若移陳小卻，使晉兵得渡，以決勝負，不亦善乎！」

translations.literal: If you would shift your lines back a little and let the Jin troops cross so that victory may be decided, would that not be better!"
translations.idiomatic: Why not pull your lines back a little and let us cross to settle the matter—would that not be better!"

sentences.zh: 秦諸將皆曰：「我眾彼寡，不如遏之，使不得上，可以萬全。」

translations.literal: All the Qin generals said: "We are many and they few—better to block them so they cannot cross; that will be completely safe."
translations.idiomatic: All the Qin generals said: "We outnumber them—better to hold them on the far bank; that is the sure course."

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「但引兵少卻，使之半渡，我以鐵騎蹙而殺之，蔑不勝矣！」

translations.literal: Fu Jian said: "Only draw the troops back a little and let them cross halfway—then we will press them with iron cavalry and slaughter them; there is nothing we cannot overcome!"
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian said: "Simply pull back a little and let them cross halfway—then we will crush them with our iron cavalry. They cannot possibly stand against us!"

sentences.zh: 融亦以為然，遂麾兵使卻。

translations.literal: Rong also thought this right and thereupon ordered the troops to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Rong agreed, and ordered the army to fall back.

sentences.zh: 秦兵遂退，不可復止，謝玄、謝琰、桓伊等引兵渡水擊之。

translations.literal: The Qin troops then retreated and could not be stopped again; Xie Xuan, Xie Yan, Huan Yi, and others led their troops across the water and attacked.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin troops fell back and could not be halted; Xie Xuan, Xie Yan, Huan Yi, and the others crossed the river and struck.

sentences.zh: 融馳騎略陳，欲以帥退者，馬倒，為晉兵所殺，秦兵遂潰。

translations.literal: Rong galloped through the lines trying to lead the retreat, but his horse fell and he was killed by Jin troops; the Qin army then collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Rong galloped along the lines trying to rally the retreat, but his horse fell and Jin troops killed him; the Qin army broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 玄等乘勝追擊，至於青岡。

translations.literal: Xuan and the others pursued in victory as far as Qinggang.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan and the others pressed the pursuit to Qinggang.

sentences.zh: 秦兵大敗，自相蹈藉而死者，蔽野塞川。

translations.literal: The Qin army was utterly defeated; those who trampled one another to death covered the fields and choked the streams.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin army was shattered; men trampled one another to death until the fields were covered and the streams choked.

sentences.zh: 其走者聞風聲鶴唳，皆以為晉兵且至，晝夜不敢息，草行露宿，重以饑凍，死者什七、八。

translations.literal: Those who fled, hearing the wind and the cries of cranes, all thought Jin troops were about to arrive; day and night they dared not rest, traveling through grass and sleeping in the dew; with hunger and cold added, seven or eight tenths of them died.
translations.idiomatic: The fugitives, hearing wind in the reeds and the cries of cranes, took every sound for advancing Jin troops; day and night they dared not rest, crawling through the grass and sleeping in the open; hunger and cold killed seven or eight out of ten.

sentences.zh: 初，秦兵小卻，朱序在陳後呼曰：「秦兵敗矣！」

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Qin troops had drawn back slightly, Zhu Xu at the rear of the lines had shouted: "The Qin army is defeated!"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as the Qin ranks fell back, Zhu Xu at the rear of the formation had shouted: "The Qin are beaten!"

sentences.zh: 眾遂大奔。

translations.literal: The masses then fled in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The army broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 序因與張天錫、徐元喜皆來奔。

translations.literal: Xu thereupon came over to the Jin side together with Zhang Tiansi and Xu Yuanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xu then defected to Jin together with Zhang Tiansi and Xu Yuanxi.

sentences.zh: 獲秦王堅所乘雲母車及儀服器械、軍資珍寶畜產不可勝計，復取壽陽，執其淮南太守郭褒。

translations.literal: They captured the mica-paneled carriage in which King Fu Jian had ridden, together with regalia, weapons, military stores, treasures, and livestock beyond counting; they recovered Shouyang and took its Huainan Administrator Guo Bao prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Fu Jian's mica-paneled carriage along with regalia, weapons, supplies, treasures, and livestock beyond reckoning; they retook Shouyang and captured Huainan administrator Guo Bao.

sentences.zh: 堅中流矢，單騎走至淮北，饑甚，民有進壺飧、豚髀者，堅食之，賜帛十匹，綿十斤。

translations.literal: Fu Jian was struck by a stray arrow and fled alone on horseback to north of the Huai; he was extremely hungry, and when a commoner brought him a pot of rice and pig's thigh, Fu Jian ate it and rewarded him with ten bolts of silk and ten jin of cotton.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian was wounded by a stray arrow and fled alone on horseback to the north bank of the Huai; starving, he accepted a pot of rice and a pig's leg from a farmer, ate, and rewarded the man with ten bolts of silk and ten jin of cotton.

sentences.zh: 辭曰：「陛下厭苦安樂，自取危困。

translations.literal: He declined, saying: "Your Majesty has wearied of ease and pleasure and brought this peril on yourself.
translations.idiomatic: He declined: "Your Majesty grew weary of ease and pleasure and brought this crisis on yourself.

sentences.zh: 臣為陛下子，陛下為臣父，安有子飼其父而求報乎？」

translations.literal: I am Your Majesty's subject and Your Majesty is my father—how could a son feed his father and then seek reward?"
translations.idiomatic: I am Your Majesty's subject and You are my sovereign—what son feeds his father and then asks for payment?"

sentences.zh: 弗顧而去。

translations.literal: Without a backward glance he went away.
translations.idiomatic: He left without looking back.

sentences.zh: 堅謂張夫人曰：「吾今復何面目治天下乎！」

translations.literal: Fu Jian said to Lady Zhang: "What face have I now to rule the realm!"
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian said to Lady Zhang: "How can I still face the task of ruling the realm!"

sentences.zh: 潸然流涕。

translations.literal: Tears streamed down his face.
translations.idiomatic: Tears streamed down his face.

sentences.zh: 是時，諸軍皆潰，惟慕容垂所將三萬人獨全，堅以千餘騎赴之。

translations.literal: At this time all the armies had collapsed; only the thirty thousand men under Murong Chui remained intact, and Fu Jian came to join him with a little more than a thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: By then every army had broken; only Murong Chui's thirty thousand men held together, and Fu Jian rode to him with barely a thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 世子寶言於垂曰：「家國傾覆，天命人心皆歸至尊，但時運未至，故晦跡自藏耳。

translations.literal: The heir apparent Bao said to Chui: "Our house and state have fallen; Heaven's mandate and men's hearts all belong to you, my lord—it is only that the time has not yet come, and so you have kept yourself in hiding.
translations.idiomatic: Heir Apparent Bao said to Chui: "Our house is ruined and Heaven's mandate is yours—only the hour had not come, and so you kept yourself concealed.

sentences.zh: 今秦主兵敗，委身於我，是天借之便以復燕祚，此時不可失也，願不以意氣微恩忘社稷之重！」

translations.literal: Now the Qin ruler's army is defeated and he has placed himself in our hands—Heaven lends us this chance to restore Yan. This moment must not be lost; do not, for a small personal debt, forget the weight of the state!"
translations.idiomatic: Now the Qin ruler is beaten and has thrown himself on our mercy—Heaven gives us this chance to restore Yan. Do not let a private kindness outweigh the fate of the realm!"

sentences.zh: 垂曰：「汝言是也。

translations.literal: Chui said: "What you say is right.
translations.idiomatic: Chui said: "You are right.

sentences.zh: 然彼以赤心投命於我，若之何害之！

translations.literal: Yet he has entrusted himself to us with a loyal heart—how can we harm him!
translations.idiomatic: Yet he came to us with a loyal heart—how can we harm him!

sentences.zh: 天苟棄之，何患不亡？

translations.literal: If Heaven has abandoned him, why worry that he will not perish?
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven has abandoned him, why fear he will not fall?

sentences.zh: 不若保護其危以報德，徐俟其釁而圖之！

translations.literal: Better to shelter him in his peril to repay his kindness, and wait for his fault before plotting against him!
translations.idiomatic: Better to protect him in his distress as repayment, and wait for his misstep before acting!

sentences.zh: 既不負宿心，且可以義取天下。」

translations.literal: Thus we neither betray our old resolve, and may yet take the realm by righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: We keep faith with our old resolve and may yet win the realm by righteousness.

sentences.zh: 奮威將軍慕容德曰：「秦強而並燕，秦弱而圖之，此為報仇雪恥，非負宿心也；

translations.literal: Striking Power General Murong De said: "When Qin was strong it swallowed Yan; when Qin is weak we plot against it—this is to avenge and wipe away shame, not to betray an old debt;
translations.idiomatic: Striking Power General Murong De said: "Qin swallowed Yan when it was strong; we strike now that it is weak—that is vengeance, not betrayal of an old debt;

sentences.zh: 兄奈何得而不取，釋數萬之眾以授人乎？」

translations.literal: Brother, why not take what is offered and release tens of thousands of troops to another's hands?"
translations.idiomatic: Brother, why release tens of thousands of men to another when you could take them?"

sentences.zh: 垂曰：「吾昔為太傅所不容，置身無所，逃死於秦，秦主以國士遇我，恩禮備至。

translations.literal: Chui said: "Long ago I was not tolerated by the Grand Tutor and had nowhere to stand; I fled death into Qin, and the Qin ruler treated me as a peer of the realm, with kindness and ritual complete.
translations.idiomatic: Chui said: "Once the Grand Tutor would not tolerate me and I had nowhere to turn; I fled into Qin, and the Qin ruler treated me as a peer of the realm with every honor.

sentences.zh: 後復為王猛所賣，無以自明。

translations.literal: Later I was betrayed by Wang Meng and could not clear myself.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wang Meng betrayed me and I could not clear my name.

sentences.zh: 秦主獨能明之，此恩何可忘也！

translations.literal: The Qin ruler alone understood me—how can this debt be forgotten!
translations.idiomatic: Only the Qin ruler understood me—how can I forget that debt!

sentences.zh: 若氐運必窮，吾當懷集關東，以復先業耳，關西會非吾有也。」

translations.literal: If the Di fate must end, I shall gather the east of the Passes to restore our former enterprise; the west of the Passes will never be mine.
translations.idiomatic: If the Di are doomed, I will rally the east of the Passes to restore our house; the west is not mine to take.

sentences.zh: 冠軍行參軍趙秋曰：「明公當紹復燕祚，著於圖讖。

translations.literal: Champion staff officer Zhao Qiu said: "My lord is destined to restore Yan, as recorded in secret prophecies.
translations.idiomatic: Champion staff officer Zhao Qiu said: "My lord is fated to restore Yan, as the prophecies record.

sentences.zh: 今天時已至，尚復何待！

translations.literal: Heaven's time has come—what are we waiting for!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's hour has come—why wait any longer!

sentences.zh: 若殺秦主，據鄴都，鼓行而西，三秦亦非苻氏之有也！」

translations.literal: If you kill the Qin ruler, hold Ye, and march west with drums beating, the Three Qins will no longer belong to the Fu clan!"
translations.idiomatic: Kill the Qin ruler, seize Ye, and march west with drums beating—the Three Qins will no longer be Fu's!"

sentences.zh: 垂親黨多勸垂殺堅，垂皆不從，悉以兵授堅。

translations.literal: Many of Chui's kin urged him to kill Fu Jian; Chui would not agree to any and gave all his troops to Fu Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Chui's kin urged him to kill Fu Jian; he refused and handed all his troops back to Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 平南將軍慕容□屯鄖城，聞堅敗，棄其眾遁去；

translations.literal: Pacify-the-South General Murong Wei (□ in source) was encamped at Yancheng; hearing of Fu Jian's defeat, he abandoned his troops and fled;
translations.idiomatic: Pacify-the-South General Murong Wei held Yancheng; when he heard of Fu Jian's defeat he abandoned his army and fled;

sentences.zh: 至滎陽，慕容德復說□起兵以復燕祚，□不從。

translations.literal: reaching Xingyang, Murong De again urged Wei to raise troops to restore Yan, but Wei would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: at Xingyang Murong De again urged Wei to raise troops to restore Yan, but Wei refused.

sentences.zh: 謝安得驛書，知秦兵已敗，時方與客圍棋，攝書置床上，了無喜色，圍棋如故。

translations.literal: Xie An received a dispatch reporting that the Qin army had been defeated; he was at the time playing go with guests, and placing the letter on the bed showed not the slightest joy, continuing the game as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie An received the dispatch reporting Qin's defeat, he was playing go with guests; he set the letter on the bed without the slightest change of expression and went on with the game.

sentences.zh: 客問之，徐答曰：「小兒輩遂已破賊。」

translations.literal: When a guest asked, he answered slowly: "The boys have already beaten the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: When a guest asked, he answered calmly: "The boys have already beaten the enemy."

sentences.zh: 既罷，還內，過戶限，不覺屐齒之折。

translations.literal: When the game ended and he returned within, crossing the threshold he did not notice that the pegs of his clogs had broken.
translations.idiomatic: When the game ended and he went inside, crossing the threshold he did not notice that the pegs of his clogs had snapped.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，謝石等歸建康，得秦樂工，能習舊聲，於是宗廟始備金石之樂。

translations.literal: On the day Dinghai, Xie Shi and others returned to Jiankang; they obtained Qin musicians who could perform the old music, and thus the ancestral temples at last had bell and stone music complete.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Dinghai, Xie Shi and others returned to Jiankang with Qin musicians who knew the old court music, and the ancestral temples at last had full bell and stone ensembles.

sentences.zh: 乙未，以張天錫為散騎常侍，朱序為琅邪內史。

translations.literal: On the day Yiwei, Zhang Tiansi was made Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary and Zhu Xu Administrator of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Yiwei, Zhang Tiansi was appointed attendant cavalier-in-ordinary and Zhu Xu administrator of Langye.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅收集離散，比至洛陽，眾十餘萬，百官、儀物，軍容粗備。

translations.literal: King Fu Jian gathered the scattered; by the time he reached Luoyang his force was more than one hundred thousand, and officials, regalia, and military appearance were roughly restored.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian gathered the scattered remnants of his army; by the time he reached Luoyang he had more than one hundred thousand men, and officials, regalia, and military order were roughly restored.

sentences.zh: 慕容農謂慕容垂曰：「尊不迫人於險，其義聲足以感動天地。

translations.literal: Murong Nong said to Murong Chui: "My lord does not press a man in peril—such righteousness is enough to move Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Nong said to Murong Chui: "You did not press a man in peril—such righteousness can move Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 農聞秘記曰：『燕復興當在河陽。』

translations.literal: Nong has heard in secret records: 'Yan's restoration will be at Heyang.'
translations.idiomatic: I have read in secret records: 'Yan will be restored at Heyang.'

sentences.zh: 夫取果於未熟與自落，不過晚旬日之間，然其難易美惡，相去遠矣！」

translations.literal: To take fruit before it is ripe or when it has fallen of itself differs by no more than ten days or so, yet the difficulty, ease, beauty, and ugliness are far apart!"
translations.idiomatic: To pluck fruit before it ripens or wait until it falls differs by barely ten days, yet the ease and the outcome are worlds apart!"

sentences.zh: 垂心善其言，行至澠池，言於堅曰：「北鄙之民，聞王師不利，輕相扇動，臣請奉詔書以鎮慰安集之，因過謁陵廟。」

translations.literal: Chui was pleased with these words; reaching Mianchi he said to Fu Jian: "The people of the northern marches, hearing that the royal army has fared ill, are lightly stirring one another; I beg to carry your edict to pacify and gather them, and on the way to visit the tombs and temples."
translations.idiomatic: Chui took his counsel to heart; at Mianchi he told Fu Jian: "The northern peoples, hearing of the army's defeat, are stirring unrest. Let me carry your edict to pacify them and, on the way, pay respects at the tombs."

sentences.zh: 堅許之。

translations.literal: Fu Jian approved.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian agreed.

sentences.zh: 權翼諫曰：「國兵新破，四方皆有離心，宜徵集名將，置之京師，以固根本，鎮枝葉。

translations.literal: Quan Yi remonstrated: "The state's army is newly defeated and all four quarters have hearts of separation; famous generals should be summoned and placed in the capital to secure the root and steady the branches.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Yi remonstrated: "The army is freshly beaten and the realm is restless; you should summon famous generals to the capital to secure the root and steady the branches.

sentences.zh: 垂勇略過人，世豪東夏，頃以避禍而來，其心豈止欲作冠軍而已哉！

translations.literal: Chui's courage and strategy surpass others; he is the great magnate of the eastern Xia; he came lately to escape disaster—does his heart aim only to be Champion General!
translations.idiomatic: Chui's courage and strategy surpass all men; he is the great magnate of the east; he came only to escape disaster—does his heart stop at being champion general!

sentences.zh: 譬如養鷹，饑則附人，每聞風飆之起，常有陵霄之志，正宜謹其絛籠，豈可解縱，任其所欲哉！」

translations.literal: It is like raising a hawk: when hungry it clings to you, but whenever it hears the wind rise it has the will to soar above the clouds—you should keep its jesses tight; how can you release it and let it do as it pleases!"
translations.idiomatic: It is like raising a hawk: hungry it clings to you, but at every rising wind it longs to soar—you must keep its jesses tight, not loose it to do as it pleases!"

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「卿言是也。

translations.literal: Fu Jian said: "Your words are right.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian said: "You are right.

sentences.zh: 然朕已許之，匹夫猶不食言，況萬乘乎？」

translations.literal: Yet I have already promised him; even a common man does not break his word—how much more a ruler of ten thousand chariots!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet I have already given my word; even a common man keeps his promise—how much more a Son of Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 若天命有廢興，固非智力所能移也。」

translations.literal: If Heaven's mandate has its rise and fall, that truly is not something wit can shift."
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven's mandate is to rise or fall, wit cannot shift it."

sentences.zh: 翼曰：「陛下重小信而輕社稷，臣見其往而不返，關東之亂，自此始矣。」

translations.literal: Yi said: "Your Majesty values small promises and undervalues the state—I see him go and not return; the turmoil of the east of the Passes begins from this."
translations.idiomatic: Yi said: "Your Majesty values a small promise over the realm—I see him leave and never return; the chaos of the east of the Passes begins here."

sentences.zh: 堅不聽，遣將軍李蠻、閔亮、尹國帥眾三千送垂。

translations.literal: Fu Jian would not listen and sent Generals Li Man, Min Liang, and Yin Guo with three thousand troops to escort Chui.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian refused and sent Generals Li Man, Min Liang, and Yin Guo with three thousand men to escort Chui.

sentences.zh: 又遣驍騎將軍石越帥精卒三千戍鄴，驃騎將軍張蚝帥羽林五千戍并州，鎮軍將軍毛當帥眾四千戌洛陽。

translations.literal: He also sent Valiant Cavalry General Shi Yue with three thousand picked troops to garrison Ye, Flying Cavalry General Zhang Hao with five thousand Feathered Forest guards to garrison Bingzhou, and Pacification Army General Mao Dang with four thousand troops to garrison Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Valiant Cavalry General Shi Yue with three thousand elite troops to garrison Ye, Flying Cavalry General Zhang Hao with five thousand Feathered Forest guards to garrison Bingzhou, and Pacification Army General Mao Dang with four thousand men to garrison Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 權翼密遣壯士邀垂於河橋南空倉中，垂疑之，自涼馬台結草筏以渡，使典軍程同衣己衣，乘己馬，與僮僕趣河橋。

translations.literal: Quan Yi secretly sent braves to ambush Chui in the empty granary south of Heqiao; Chui grew suspicious, lashed rafts of grass at Liangmatai to cross, and had army officer Cheng Tong wear his clothes and ride his horse with servants toward Heqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Yi secretly sent men to ambush Chui in the empty granary south of Heqiao; Chui grew suspicious, rafted across at Liangmatai, and had Cheng Tong wear his clothes and ride his horse toward the bridge with servants.

sentences.zh: 伏兵發，同馳馬獲免。

translations.literal: The ambush sprang; Tong galloped free.
translations.idiomatic: The ambush sprang; Tong galloped through and escaped.

sentences.zh: 十二月，秦王堅至長安，哭陽平公融而後入，謚曰哀公。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month King Fu Jian reached Chang'an, wept for the Duke of Yangping Fu Rong and then entered, and gave him the posthumous title Duke Ai.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month King Fu Jian reached Chang'an, mourned the Duke of Yangping Fu Rong, and then entered the city, posthumously titling him Duke Ai.

sentences.zh: 大赦，復死事者家。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed and families of those who died in service were restored.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed and the families of the war dead were restored.

sentences.zh: 庚午，大赦。

translations.literal: On the day Gengwu a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Gengwu a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 以謝石為尚書令。

translations.literal: Xie Shi was made Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shi was appointed director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 進謝玄號前將軍，固讓不受。

translations.literal: Xie Xuan was advanced to Forward General but firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xuan was offered the title Forward General but firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 謝安婿王國寶，坦之之子也；

translations.literal: Wang Guobao, son-in-law of Xie An, was the son of Tan Zhi;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guobao, Xie An's son-in-law, was Tan Zhi's son;

sentences.zh: 安惡其為人，每抑而不用，以為尚書郎。

translations.literal: An disliked his character and always held him back from office, making him a Masters of Writing gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: An disliked his character and always held him back, appointing him only a gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 國寶自以望族，故事唯作吏部，不為餘曹，固辭不拜，由是怨安。

translations.literal: Guobao, considering himself of an eminent clan, held that by precedent one served only in the Ministry of Personnel and not in other bureaus; he firmly declined appointment and thereby resented An.
translations.idiomatic: Guobao, counting himself of an eminent clan, held that by precedent one served only in the Ministry of Personnel; he refused other posts and came to resent An.

sentences.zh: 國寶從妹為會稽王道子妃，帝與道子皆嗜酒，狎暱邪諂，國寶乃譖安於道子，使離間之於帝。

translations.literal: Guobao's cousin on his mother's side was consort to the Prince of Kuaiji, Sima Daozi; the emperor and Daozi both loved wine and were intimate with flatterers and sycophants; Guobao then slandered An to Daozi and set him to sow discord with the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Guobao's cousin was consort to the Prince of Kuaiji, Sima Daozi; emperor and prince both loved wine and kept company with flatterers; Guobao slandered An to Daozi and set him to alienate the emperor.

sentences.zh: 安功名既盛，而險詖求進之徒，多毀短安，帝由是稍疏忌之。

translations.literal: An's fame and achievement were already great, and men who were crafty and sought advancement by crooked paths many spoke ill of An; the emperor therefore gradually grew distant and wary of him.
translations.idiomatic: An's fame was already towering, and crafty men seeking advancement spoke ill of him; the emperor gradually grew distant and wary.

sentences.zh: 初開酒禁，增民稅米，口五石。

translations.literal: For the first time a prohibition on wine was enacted and the people's grain tax was increased to five piculs per mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Wine was banned for the first time and the grain tax was raised to five piculs per person.

sentences.zh: 秦呂光行越流沙三百餘里，焉耆等諸國皆降。

translations.literal: Lü Guang of Qin marched more than three hundred li across the drifting sands; the states of Yanqi and others all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang of Qin marched more than three hundred li across the drifting sands; Yanqi and the other states all submitted.

sentences.zh: 惟龜茲王帛純拒之，嬰城固守，光進軍攻之。

translations.literal: Only King Bochun of Kucha resisted; he closed the city and held firm while Guang advanced to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Only King Bochun of Kucha resisted, shutting the gates while Guang besieged the city.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅之入寇也，以乞伏國仁為前將軍，領先鋒騎。

translations.literal: When King Fu Jian invaded, he made Qifu Guoren Forward General in command of the vanguard cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When King Fu Jian invaded, he made Qifu Guoren forward general commanding the vanguard cavalry.

sentences.zh: 會國仁叔父步頹反於隴西，堅遣國仁還討之。

translations.literal: When Guoren's uncle Bufei rebelled in Longxi, Fu Jian sent Guoren back to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When Guoren's uncle Bufei rebelled in Longxi, Fu Jian sent Guoren to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 步頹聞之，大喜，迎國仁於路。

translations.literal: Bufei heard this and was greatly pleased, meeting Guoren on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Bufei was delighted and met Guoren on the road.

sentences.zh: 國仁置酒，大言曰：「苻氏疲民逞兵，殆將亡矣，吾當與諸君共建一方之業。」

translations.literal: Guoren set out wine and spoke boldly: "The Fu clan weary the people and wield arms—they will soon perish; I shall with you all build an enterprise in our own region."
translations.idiomatic: Guoren set out wine and declared boldly: "The Fu clan exhaust the people with war—they are nearly finished; I shall build a realm here with you all."

sentences.zh: 及堅敗，國仁遂迫脅諸部，有不從者，擊而並之，眾至十餘萬。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian was defeated, Guoren then coerced the various tribes; those who would not submit he attacked and absorbed, until his force reached more than one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian was defeated, Guoren coerced the tribes, absorbing by force any who refused, until his following reached more than one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂至安陽，遣參軍田山修箋於長樂公丕。

translations.literal: Murong Chui reached Anyang and sent staff officer Tian Shan with a letter to the Duke of Changle, Fu Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui reached Anyang and sent staff officer Tian Shan with a letter to the Duke of Changle, Fu Pi.

sentences.zh: 丕聞垂北來，疑其欲為亂，然猶身自迎之。

translations.literal: When Pi heard that Chui was coming north he suspected he meant to make trouble, yet still went out in person to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: Pi heard Chui was coming north and suspected revolt, yet went out in person to meet him.

sentences.zh: 趙秋勸垂於座取丕，因據鄴起兵，垂不從。

translations.literal: Zhao Qiu urged Chui to seize Pi at the meeting and thereupon raise troops at Ye; Chui would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Qiu urged Chui to seize Pi at the meeting and raise troops at Ye; Chui refused.

sentences.zh: 丕謀襲擊垂，侍郎天水姜讓諫曰：「垂反形未著，而明公擅殺之，非臣子之義；

translations.literal: Pi plotted to strike Chui; Gentleman of the Palace Jiang Rang of Tianshui remonstrated: "Chui's rebellious intent is not yet manifest, yet my lord would kill him on your own authority—that is not the duty of a subject;
translations.idiomatic: Pi plotted to attack Chui; Gentleman of the Palace Jiang Rang of Tianshui said: "Chui's treason is not yet plain, yet you would kill him on your own authority—that is not a subject's duty;

sentences.zh: 不如待以上賓之禮，嚴兵衛之，密表情狀，聽敕而後圖之。」

translations.literal: better to treat him as an honored guest, guard him strictly, report his conduct in secret, and act only after receiving orders."
translations.idiomatic: better to treat him as an honored guest, guard him closely, report his conduct, and act only on imperial command."

sentences.zh: 丕從之，館垂於鄴西。

translations.literal: Pi agreed and lodged Chui west of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Pi agreed and lodged Chui west of Ye.

sentences.zh: 垂潛與燕之故臣謀復燕祚，會丁零翟斌起兵叛秦，謀攻豫州牧平原公暉於洛陽，秦王堅驛書使垂將兵討之。

translations.literal: Chui secretly plotted with former Yan ministers to restore Yan; when the Dingling leader Zhai Bin raised troops in rebellion against Qin and plotted to attack the Governor of Yuzhou, the Duke of Pingyuan Fu Hui, at Luoyang, King Fu Jian sent Chui by dispatch to lead troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: Chui secretly plotted with former Yan ministers to restore the house; when Zhai Bin of the Dingling rebelled and moved against Fu Hui at Luoyang, Fu Jian ordered Chui to lead troops against him.

sentences.zh: 石越言於丕曰：「王師新敗，民心未安，負罪亡匿之徒，思亂者眾，故丁零一唱，旬日之中，眾已數千，此其驗也。

translations.literal: Shi Yue said to Pi: "The royal army is newly defeated and the people's hearts are not settled; men who have fled guilt and hidden themselves, desiring turmoil, are many—thus at Zhai Bin's first call, within ten days his force was already several thousand; this is the proof.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yue told Pi: "The royal army is freshly beaten and the people are unsettled; fugitives and malcontents are everywhere—Zhai Bin's call drew thousands in ten days; that is the proof.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂，燕之宿望，有興復舊業之心。

translations.literal: Murong Chui is Yan's old pillar and has the heart to restore the former enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui is Yan's old pillar and burns to restore the realm.

sentences.zh: 今復資之以兵，此為虎傅翼也。」

translations.literal: Now to supply him again with troops is to give wings to a tiger."
translations.idiomatic: To arm him again is to give wings to a tiger."

sentences.zh: 丕曰：「垂在鄴如藉虎寢蛟，常恐為肘腋之變。

translations.literal: Pi said: "Chui at Ye is like a tiger resting or a dragon sleeping—we constantly fear trouble at the elbow.
translations.idiomatic: Pi said: "Chui at Ye is like a tiger in our bed—we fear him at our elbow.

sentences.zh: 今遠之於外，不猶愈乎！

translations.literal: To send him far away—is that not better!
translations.idiomatic: To send him far away—is that not better!

sentences.zh: 且翟斌凶悖，必不肯為垂下，使兩虎相斃，吾從而制之，此卞莊子之術也。」

translations.literal: Moreover Zhai Bin is fierce and perverse and will surely not serve under Chui; let two tigers destroy each other and we take control afterward—this is Bian Zhuangzi's stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Bin is fierce and will not serve under Chui; let two tigers fight and we control the aftermath—Bian Zhuangzi's stratagem."

sentences.zh: 乃以羸兵二千及鎧仗之弊者給垂，又遣廣武將軍苻飛龍帥氐騎一千為垂之副，密戒飛龍曰：「垂為三軍之帥，卿為謀垂之將，行矣，勉之！」

translations.literal: Thereupon he gave Chui two thousand weak troops and worn armor and weapons, and also sent Valiant Martial General Fu Feilong with one thousand Di cavalry as Chui's deputy, secretly instructing Feilong: "Chui is commander of the three armies; you are the general who plots against Chui—go, and exert yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: He gave Chui two thousand weak troops and worn gear, and sent Valiant Martial General Fu Feilong with one thousand Di horse as deputy, secretly telling Feilong: "Chui commands the army; you are to plot against him—go, and do your utmost!"

sentences.zh: 垂請入鄴城拜廟，丕弗許，乃潛服而入；

translations.literal: Chui asked to enter Ye city to worship at the ancestral temple; Pi would not permit it, so Chui dressed secretly and entered;
translations.idiomatic: Chui asked to enter Ye to worship at the temple; Pi refused, so Chui entered in disguise;

sentences.zh: 亭吏禁之，垂怒，斬吏燒亭而去。

translations.literal: the post-house clerk barred him; Chui in anger beheaded the clerk, burned the post, and left.
translations.idiomatic: a post-house clerk barred him; Chui in anger killed the clerk, burned the post, and left.

sentences.zh: 石越言於丕曰：「垂敢輕侮方鎮，殺吏燒亭，反形已露，可因此除之。」

translations.literal: Shi Yue said to Pi: "The royal army is newly defeated and the people's hearts are not settled; men who have fled guilt and hidden themselves, desiring turmoil, are many—thus at Zhai Bin's first call, within ten days his force was already several thousand; this is the proof."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yue told Pi: "The royal army is freshly beaten and the people are unsettled; fugitives and malcontents are everywhere—Zhai Bin's call drew thousands in ten days; that is the proof."

sentences.zh: 丕曰：「淮南之敗，垂侍衛乘輿，此功不可忘也。」

translations.literal: Pi said: "At the defeat at Huainan, Chui guarded the imperial carriage—this merit cannot be forgotten."
translations.idiomatic: Pi said: "At Huainan he guarded the imperial carriage—that debt cannot be forgotten."

sentences.zh: 越曰：「垂尚不忠於燕，安能盡忠於我？

translations.literal: Yue said: "If Chui was not loyal to Yan, how can he be wholly loyal to us!
translations.idiomatic: Yue said: "If he was not loyal to Yan, how can he be loyal to us!

sentences.zh: 失今不取，必為後患。」

translations.literal: If we do not take him now, he will surely be a later trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Miss this chance and he will be a lasting trouble."

sentences.zh: 丕不從。

translations.literal: Pi would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Pi refused.

sentences.zh: 越退，告人曰：「公父子好為小仁，不顧大計，終當為人擒耳。」

translations.literal: Yue withdrew and told others: "The lord and son favor small kindness and disregard the great plan—they will in the end be captured by others."
translations.idiomatic: Yue withdrew and said: "Father and son favor small kindness over the great plan—they will end captured by others."

sentences.zh: 垂留慕容農、慕容楷、慕容紹於鄴，行至安陽之湯池，閔亮、李毘自鄴來，以丕與苻飛龍所謀告垂。

translations.literal: Chui left Murong Nong, Murong Kai, and Murong Shao at Ye; reaching the hot springs of Anyang, Min Liang and Li Pi came from Ye and told Chui of Pi's plot with Fu Feilong.
translations.idiomatic: Chui left Murong Nong, Murong Kai, and Murong Shao at Ye; at Anyang's hot springs Min Liang and Li Pi came from Ye and revealed Pi's plot with Fu Feilong.

sentences.zh: 垂因激怒其眾曰：「吾盡忠於苻氏，而彼專欲圖吾父子，吾雖欲已，得乎！

translations.literal: Chui thereupon roused his troops in anger, saying: "I have served the Fu clan with full loyalty, yet they plot solely against me and my sons—though I wished to stop, can I!
translations.idiomatic: Chui roused his troops: "I served the Fu clan faithfully, yet they plot against me and my sons—I cannot hold back!

sentences.zh: 乃託言兵少，停河內募兵，旬日間，有眾八千。

translations.literal: He then claimed his troops were few, halted at Henei to levy soldiers, and within ten days had eight thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed his force was small, halted at Henei to levy troops, and within ten days had eight thousand men.

sentences.zh: 平原公暉遣使讓垂，趣使進兵。

translations.literal: The Duke of Pingyuan Fu Hui sent a messenger to reproach Chui and urge him to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Hui sent a messenger to reproach Chui and urge him forward.

sentences.zh: 垂謂飛龍曰：「今寇賊不遠，當晝止夜行，襲其不意。」

translations.literal: Chui said to Feilong: "The bandits are not far; we should halt by day and march by night to strike them unawares."
translations.idiomatic: Chui told Feilong: "The enemy is near—we should march by night and strike unawares."

sentences.zh: 飛龍以為然。

translations.literal: Feilong thought this right.
translations.idiomatic: Feilong agreed.

sentences.zh: 壬午，夜，垂遣世子寶將兵居前，少子隆勒兵從己，令氐兵五人為伍；

translations.literal: On the day Renwu, at night, Chui sent Heir Apparent Bao to lead troops in front, his youngest son Long to command troops following him, and ordered Di soldiers in groups of five;
translations.idiomatic: On the night of Renwu, Chui sent Heir Apparent Bao ahead, his son Long following, with Di troops in groups of five;

sentences.zh: 陰與寶約，聞鼓聲，前後合擊氐兵及飛龍，盡殺之，參佐家在西者皆遣還，並以書遺秦王堅，言所以殺飛龍之故。

translations.literal: secretly agreeing with Bao that at the sound of drums they would strike front and rear together at the Di troops and Feilong, killing them all; staff whose families were in the west were all sent home, and a letter was also sent to King Fu Jian explaining why Feilong was killed.
translations.idiomatic: secretly agreeing with Bao that at the drum they would strike the Di and Feilong from front and rear, killing them all; western staff were sent home, and a letter was sent to Fu Jian explaining why Feilong was killed.

sentences.zh: 初，垂從堅入鄴，以其子麟屢嘗告變於燕，立殺其母，然猶不忍殺麟，置之外捨，希得侍見。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chui followed Fu Jian into Ye, because his son Lin had repeatedly reported plots to Yan, he had immediately killed Lin's mother, yet still could not bear to kill Lin and placed him in an outer lodge, hoping occasionally to see him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Chui followed Fu Jian into Ye, because his son Lin had repeatedly informed on Yan, he killed Lin's mother at once yet spared Lin, keeping him in an outer lodge.

sentences.zh: 乃殺苻飛龍，麟屢進策畫，啟發垂意，垂更奇之，寵待與諸子均矣。

translations.literal: After killing Fu Feilong, Lin repeatedly offered plans that stirred Chui's intent; Chui marveled at him all the more and favored him equally with his other sons.
translations.idiomatic: After killing Fu Feilong, Lin repeatedly offered plans that stirred Chui's thinking; Chui marveled at him and favored him like his other sons.

sentences.zh: 慕容鳳及燕故臣之子燕郡王騰、遼西段延等聞翟斌起兵，各帥部曲歸之。

translations.literal: Murong Feng and the sons of former Yan ministers—the Prince of Yancheng Teng, Liaoxi Duan Yan, and others—hearing that Zhai Bin had raised troops, each led their personal followings to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Feng, Prince of Yancheng Teng, Duan Yan of Liaoxi, and others, hearing of Zhai Bin's rising, each led their followings to join him.

sentences.zh: 平原公暉使武平武侯毛當討斌。

translations.literal: The Duke of Pingyuan, Fu Hui, sent the Marquis of Wupinghou, Mao Dang, to attack Zhai Bin.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Pingyuan, Fu Hui, dispatched the Marquis of Wupinghou, Mao Dang, to suppress Zhai Bin.

sentences.zh: 慕容鳳曰：「鳳今將雪先王之恥，請為斬此氐奴。」

translations.literal: Murong Feng said: "Feng will now wipe away the shame of our former kings; please let me behead this Di slave."
translations.idiomatic: Murong Feng said: "I mean to avenge the humiliation of our former kings—let me cut down this Di wretch."

sentences.zh: 乃擐甲直進，丁零之眾隨之，大敗秦兵，斬毛當；

translations.literal: Then he donned armor and charged straight ahead; the Dingling masses followed, and they routed the Qin army and beheaded Mao Dang;
translations.idiomatic: He buckled on his armor and charged straight in; the Dingling warriors followed, and they routed the Qin forces and killed Mao Dang;

sentences.zh: 遂進攻陵雲台戍，克之，收萬餘人甲仗。

translations.literal: Then they pressed the attack on the Lingyun Terrace garrison, captured it, and seized armor and weapons for more than ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: They then stormed the Lingyun Terrace garrison, took it, and captured enough arms and armor to equip more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 癸未，慕容垂濟河焚橋，有眾三萬，留遼東鮮卑可足渾潭集兵於河內之沙城。

translations.literal: On the day Guiwei, Murong Chui crossed the river and burned the bridges; he had thirty thousand followers and left the Liaodong Xianbei Kezuhun Tan to gather troops at Shacheng in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Guiwei, Murong Chui crossed the Yellow River and burned the bridges behind him. He had thirty thousand men with him and left the Liaodong Xianbei Kezuhun Tan to raise troops at Shacheng in Henei.

sentences.zh: 垂遣田山如鄴，密告慕容農等使起兵相應。

translations.literal: Chui sent Tian Shan to Ye to secretly tell Murong Nong and the others to raise troops in response.
translations.idiomatic: Chui sent Tian Shan to Ye with a secret message urging Murong Nong and the others to rise in support.

sentences.zh: 時日已暮，農與慕容楷留宿鄴中；

translations.literal: By then dusk had fallen; Nong and Murong Kai stayed overnight in Ye;
translations.idiomatic: Night had already fallen, so Nong and Murong Kai lodged overnight in Ye;

sentences.zh: 慕容紹先出，至蒲池，盜丕駿馬數百匹以待農、楷。

translations.literal: Murong Shao went out first to Pu Pool, stole several hundred of Fu Pi's fine horses, and waited for Nong and Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Shao slipped out first to Pu Pool, stole several hundred of Fu Pi's best horses, and waited there for Nong and Kai.

sentences.zh: 甲申晦，農、楷將數十騎微服出鄴，遂同奔列人。

translations.literal: On the last day of the month, the day Jiashen, Nong and Kai led several dozen horsemen in plain dress out of Ye and together fled to Lieren.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the month, the day Jiashen, Nong and Kai rode out of Ye with a few dozen men in disguise and fled together to Lieren.

sentences.zh: 烈宗孝武皇帝上之下太元九年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, first part lower section, ninth year of Taiyuan (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, lower fascicle of the first part, ninth year of Taiyuan (

sentences.zh: 甲申，公元三八四年）

translations.literal: Jiashen, AD 384)
translations.idiomatic: the day Jiashen, AD 384)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙酉朔，秦長樂公丕大會賓客，請慕容農不得，始覺有變。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the new-moon day Yiyou, the Duke of Changle of Qin, Fu Pi, held a grand gathering of guests and invited Murong Nong, but could not get him to come—only then did he realize something was amiss.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the new moon of the day Yiyou, Fu Pi, Duke of Changle of Qin, held a great banquet for his guests and sent for Murong Nong, but Nong did not come. Only then did Pi sense that something was wrong.

sentences.zh: 遣人四出求之，三日，乃知其在列人，已起兵矣。

translations.literal: He sent men out in all directions to seek him; after three days he learned that Nong was at Lieren and had already raised troops.
translations.idiomatic: He sent men searching in every direction; three days later he learned that Nong was at Lieren and had already taken up arms.

sentences.zh: 慕容鳳、王騰、段延皆勸翟斌奉慕容垂為盟主；

translations.literal: Murong Feng, Wang Teng, and Duan Yan all urged Zhai Bin to take Murong Chui as alliance leader;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Feng, Wang Teng, and Duan Yan all urged Zhai Bin to accept Murong Chui as leader of the alliance;

sentences.zh: 斌從之。

translations.literal: Bin agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Bin agreed.

sentences.zh: 垂欲襲洛陽，且未知斌之誠偽，乃拒之曰：「吾來救豫州，不來赴君。

translations.literal: Chui intended to strike at Luoyang and did not yet know whether Bin's intent was genuine or feigned, so he declined, saying: "I came to rescue Yuzhou, not to answer your summons.
translations.idiomatic: Chui meant to strike at Luoyang and still could not tell whether Bin's overture was sincere, so he refused him, saying: "I came to save Yuzhou, not to answer your call.

sentences.zh: 君既建大事，成享其福，敗受其禍，吾無預焉。」

translations.literal: You have launched a great enterprise—if it succeeds you will enjoy the reward, if it fails you will bear the disaster; I have no part in it.
translations.idiomatic: You have raised a great cause: if it succeeds, you will reap the reward; if it fails, you will bear the ruin. I want no share in it.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，垂至洛陽，平原公暉聞其殺苻飛龍，閉門拒之。

translations.literal: On the day Bingxu, Chui reached Luoyang; the Duke of Pingyuan, Fu Hui, hearing that he had killed Fu Feilong, shut the gates and barred him.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Bingxu, Chui reached Luoyang. The Duke of Pingyuan, Fu Hui, learning that Chui had killed Fu Feilong, shut the gates and refused him entry.

sentences.zh: 翟斌復遣長史郭通往說垂，垂猶未許。

translations.literal: Zhai Bin again sent Chief Clerk Guo Tong to persuade Chui, but Chui still did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Bin sent Chief Clerk Guo Tong again to win Chui over, but Chui still held back.

sentences.zh: 通曰：「將軍所以拒通者，豈非以翟斌兄弟山野異類，無奇才遠略，必無所成故邪？

translations.literal: Tong said: "The reason the general refuses Tong—is it not because the Zhai Bin brothers are wild mountain folk of a different kind, without extraordinary talent or far-reaching strategy, and are sure to accomplish nothing?
translations.idiomatic: Tong said: "Does the general refuse me because he thinks the Zhai Bin brothers are crude mountaineers of another stock, without great talent or long vision, and bound to fail?

sentences.zh: 獨不念將軍今日憑之，可以濟大業乎！」

translations.literal: Do you not consider that by relying on them today the general can still accomplish the great enterprise!"
translations.idiomatic: Has the general forgotten that, for all that, he needs them now if he is to finish the great work!"

sentences.zh: 垂乃許之。

translations.literal: Then Chui agreed.
translations.idiomatic: At that Chui consented.

sentences.zh: 於是斌帥其眾來與垂會，勸垂稱尊號。

translations.literal: Thereupon Bin led his followers to meet with Chui and urged Chui to assume a supreme title.
translations.idiomatic: Bin then brought his followers to join Chui and urged him to take a royal title.

sentences.zh: 垂曰：「新興侯，吾主也，當迎歸返正耳。」

translations.literal: Chui said: "The Marquis of Xinxing is my lord; I should welcome him back and restore the proper rule."
translations.idiomatic: Chui said: "The Marquis of Xinxing is my sovereign. I mean only to bring him home and restore legitimate rule."

sentences.zh: 垂以洛陽四面受敵，欲取鄴而據之，乃引兵而東。

translations.literal: Because Luoyang was threatened on all sides, Chui wished to take Ye and hold it, so he led his army east.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang was exposed on every side, so Chui decided to seize Ye and make it his base, and marched east.

sentences.zh: 故扶餘王餘蔚為滎陽太守，及昌黎鮮卑衛駒各帥其眾降垂。

translations.literal: The former king of Fuyu, Yu Wei, who was governor of Xingyang, and the Changli Xianbei Wei Ju each led their followers to surrender to Chui.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wei, the former king of Fuyu and governor of Xingyang, and the Changli Xianbei Wei Ju each came over to Chui with their followers.

sentences.zh: 垂至滎陽，群下固請上尊號，垂乃依晉中宗故事，稱大將軍、大都督、燕王，承製行事，謂之統府。

translations.literal: When Chui reached Xingyang, his subordinates repeatedly pressed him to assume a supreme title; Chui then followed the precedent of Jin's Zhongzong, declaring himself Grand General, Grand Commander, and Prince of Yan, acting by imperial decree—this was called the Unified Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At Xingyang his officers pressed him again to take a royal title. Chui followed the Jin Zhongzong precedent, styling himself Grand General, Grand Commander, and Prince of Yan and governing by decree under what was called the Unified Commandery.

sentences.zh: 群下稱臣，文表奏誥，封拜官爵，皆如王者。

translations.literal: His subordinates addressed him as ministers; memorials, reports, and edicts, enfeoffments and appointments—all were as for a king.
translations.idiomatic: His followers addressed him as their lord; memorials, reports, edicts, enfeoffments, and appointments all followed royal practice.

sentences.zh: 以弟德為車騎大將軍，封范陽王；

translations.literal: He appointed his brother De Grand Chariot-and-Cavalry General and enfeoffed him as Prince of Fanyang;
translations.idiomatic: He made his brother Murong De Grand Chariot-and-Cavalry General and Prince of Fanyang;

sentences.zh: 兄子楷為征西大將軍，封太原王；

translations.literal: His brother's son Kai as Campaign-West Grand General and Prince of Taiyuan;
translations.idiomatic: his nephew Murong Kai Campaign-West Grand General and Prince of Taiyuan;

sentences.zh: 翟斌為建義大將軍，封河南王；

translations.literal: Zhai Bin as Establish-the-Cause Grand General and Prince of Henan;
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Bin Establish-the-Cause Grand General and Prince of Henan;

sentences.zh: 餘蔚為征東將軍，統府左司馬，封扶餘王；

translations.literal: Yu Wei as Campaign-East General, Left Chief Administrator of the Unified Commandery, and Prince of Fuyu;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wei Campaign-East General, Left Chief Administrator of the Unified Commandery, and Prince of Fuyu;

sentences.zh: 衛駒為鷹揚將軍，慕容鳳為建策將軍。

translations.literal: Wei Ju as Striking Eagle General and Murong Feng as Establish-the-Plan General.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ju Striking Eagle General and Murong Feng Establish-the-Plan General.

sentences.zh: 帥眾二十餘萬，自石門濟河，長驅向鄴。

translations.literal: He led more than two hundred thousand men, crossed the river at Shimen, and drove straight toward Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He marched more than two hundred thousand men across the river at Shimen and swept toward Ye.

sentences.zh: 慕容農之奔列人也，止於烏桓魯利家，利為之置饌，農笑而不食。

translations.literal: When Murong Nong fled to Lieren, he stopped at the home of the Wuhuan Luli; Luli set out a meal for him, but Nong smiled and did not eat.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Nong fled to Lieren, he stopped at the house of the Wuhuan Luli. Luli laid out a meal for him, but Nong only smiled and would not eat.

sentences.zh: 利謂其妻曰：「惡奴，郎貴人，家貧無以饌之，奈何？」

translations.literal: Luli said to his wife: "You wretched slave—the young lord is a nobleman, and our house is too poor to entertain him properly; what are we to do?
translations.idiomatic: Luli said to his wife: "You worthless woman—the young lord is a man of rank, and we are too poor to feed him properly. What can we do?

sentences.zh: 妻曰：「郎有雄才大志，今無故而至，必將有異，非為飲食來也。

translations.literal: His wife said: "The young lord has heroic talent and great ambition; his coming here now without apparent cause surely means something extraordinary—he has not come merely for food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: She said: "This young lord has great talent and ambition. He has come here for no ordinary reason; he did not come merely to eat.

sentences.zh: 君亟出，遠望以備非常。」

translations.literal: Husband, go out at once and keep watch from afar against anything unforeseen."
translations.idiomatic: Go out at once and keep watch from a distance against anything unexpected."

sentences.zh: 利從之。

translations.literal: Luli did as she said.
translations.idiomatic: Luli did as she said.

sentences.zh: 農謂利曰：「吾欲集兵列人以圖興復，卿能從我乎？」

translations.literal: Nong said to Luli: "I wish to gather troops at Lieren to plot restoration—can you follow me?
translations.idiomatic: Nong said to Luli: "I mean to raise an army at Lieren and work for restoration. Will you follow me?

sentences.zh: 利曰：「死生唯郎是從。」

translations.literal: Luli said: "In life or death I follow the young lord alone."
translations.idiomatic: Luli said: "In life or death I follow you alone."

sentences.zh: 農乃詣烏桓張驤，說之曰：「家王已舉大事，翟斌等鹹相推奉，遠近響應，故來相告耳。」

translations.literal: Nong then went to the Wuhuan Zhang Rang and persuaded him: "Our family's king has already launched the great enterprise; Zhai Bin and the rest have all pledged support, and responses have come from far and near—I have come only to inform you."
translations.idiomatic: Nong then went to the Wuhuan Zhang Rang and told him: "Our prince has already risen. Zhai Bin and the others have all pledged themselves to him, and support is pouring in from every side. I have come only to tell you."

sentences.zh: 驤再拜曰：「得舊主而奉之，敢不盡死！」

translations.literal: Rang bowed twice and said: "To obtain our old lord and serve him—how dare I not give my utmost unto death!"
translations.idiomatic: Rang bowed twice and said: "If I can serve our old lord again, how could I not give my life for him!"

sentences.zh: 於是農驅列人居民為士卒，斬桑榆為兵，裂襜裳為旗，使趙秋說屠各畢聰。

translations.literal: Thereupon Nong drove the people of Lieren as soldiers, cut mulberry and elm for weapons, tore skirts for banners, and sent Zhao Qiu to persuade the Tuge chief Bi Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Nong then pressed the people of Lieren into service as soldiers, cut mulberry and elm for spears, tore skirts into flags, and sent Zhao Qiu to win over the Tuge chief Bi Cong.

sentences.zh: 聰與屠各卜勝、張延、李白、郭超及東夷餘和、敕勒、易陽烏桓劉大各帥部眾數千赴之。

translations.literal: Cong, together with the Tuge Pu Sheng, Zhang Yan, Li Bai, Guo Chao, the Dongyi Yu He, the Chile, and the Yiyang Wuhuan Liu Da, each leading several thousand of their followers, came to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Cong came, and with him the Tuge Pu Sheng, Zhang Yan, Li Bai, Guo Chao, the Dongyi Yu He, the Chile, and the Yiyang Wuhuan Liu Da, each at the head of several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 農假張驤輔國將軍，劉大安遠將軍，魯利建威將軍。

translations.literal: Nong provisionally appointed Zhang Rang Assistant-State General, Liu Da Pacify-the-Distance General, and Luli Establish-Power General.
translations.idiomatic: Nong made Zhang Rang acting Assistant-State General, Liu Da acting Pacify-the-Distance General, and Luli acting Establish-Power General.

sentences.zh: 農自將攻破館陶，收其軍資器械，遣蘭汗、段贊、趙秋、慕輿悕略取康台牧馬數千匹。

translations.literal: Nong personally led the attack and captured Guantao, seizing its military stores and equipment; he sent Lan Han, Duan Zan, Zhao Qiu, and Muyu Xi to raid and take several thousand horses from the pasture at Kangtai.
translations.idiomatic: Nong himself led the capture of Guantao and took its stores and weapons. He sent Lan Han, Duan Zan, Zhao Qiu, and Muyu Xi to seize several thousand horses from the pastures at Kangtai.

sentences.zh: 汗，燕王垂之從舅；

translations.literal: Han was Prince of Yan Murong Chui's maternal uncle;
translations.idiomatic: Lan Han was Murong Chui's maternal uncle;

sentences.zh: 贊，聰之子也。

translations.literal: Zan was Cong's son.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Zan was Bi Cong's son.

sentences.zh: 於是步騎雲集，眾至數萬，驤等共推農為使持節、都督河北諸軍事、驃騎大將軍，監統諸將，隨才部署，上下肅然。
