translations.literal: Thereupon infantry and cavalry gathered like clouds until the force reached tens of thousands; Rang and the rest jointly recommended Nong as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Area Commander of all Military Affairs north of the Yellow River, and Flying Cavalry Grand General, supervising and commanding all the generals, appointing each according to his talent—the whole force was orderly from top to bottom.
translations.idiomatic: Foot and horse then gathered until his force numbered in the tens of thousands. Rang and the others jointly made Nong Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander of all Military Affairs north of the Yellow River, and Flying Cavalry Grand General, with authority over every general and appointments made according to merit. The whole army was disciplined from top to bottom.

sentences.zh: 農以燕王垂未至，不敢封賞將士。

translations.literal: Because Prince of Yan Murong Chui had not yet arrived, Nong did not dare enfeoff or reward the officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Because Murong Chui had not yet arrived, Nong did not dare grant titles or rewards to the troops.

sentences.zh: 趙秋曰：「軍無賞，士不往。

translations.literal: Zhao Qiu said: "An army without rewards—soldiers will not come.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Qiu said: "An army without rewards will not keep its men.

sentences.zh: 今之來者，皆欲建一時之功，規萬世之利，宜承製封拜，以廣中興之基。」

translations.literal: Those who come now all wish to achieve merit for the moment and plan advantage for ten thousand generations—you should act by decree to enfeoff and appoint, to broaden the foundation of restoration."
translations.idiomatic: Those who join us now want immediate glory and lasting gain. You should issue appointments under royal authority and broaden the foundation of restoration."

sentences.zh: 農從之，於是赴者相繼；

translations.literal: Nong agreed, and from then on those who came did so in succession;
translations.idiomatic: Nong agreed, and from then on recruits kept arriving in a steady stream;

sentences.zh: 垂聞而善之。

translations.literal: Chui heard of it and approved.
translations.idiomatic: When Chui heard of it, he approved.

sentences.zh: 農西招庫辱官偉於上黨，東引乞特歸於東阿，北召光烈將軍平睿及睿兄汝陽太守幼於燕國；

translations.literal: Nong recruited to the west Kuru Official Wei in Shangdang, drew to the east Jite Gui at Dong'e, and summoned to the north Resplendent Virtue General Ping Rui and Rui's elder brother, Governor of Ruyang, You, in the Yan region;
translations.idiomatic: Nong summoned Kuru Official Wei in Shangdang to the west, drew Jite Gui to Dong'e in the east, and called north to Resplendent Virtue General Ping Rui and Rui's elder brother Ping You, governor of Ruyang, in the Yan region;

sentences.zh: 偉等皆應之。

translations.literal: Wei and the others all responded.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and the others all answered his call.

sentences.zh: 又遣蘭汗等攻頓丘，克之。

translations.literal: He also sent Lan Han and the others to attack Duniu and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Lan Han and the others against Duniu and took it.

sentences.zh: 農號令整肅，軍無私掠，士女喜悅。

translations.literal: Nong's orders were strict and orderly; the army engaged in no private plunder, and men and women rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Nong's discipline was strict; his army did not loot, and the people welcomed them.

sentences.zh: 長樂公丕使石越將步騎萬餘討之。

translations.literal: The Duke of Changle, Fu Pi, sent Shi Yue at the head of more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi, Duke of Changle, sent Shi Yue with more than ten thousand foot and horse to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 農曰：「越有智勇之名，今不南拒大軍而來此，是畏王而陵我也；

translations.literal: Nong said: "Yue has a reputation for wisdom and valor; that he does not turn south to block the main army but comes here shows he fears the Prince and looks down on me—
translations.idiomatic: Nong said: "Yue has a name for wisdom and courage. If he does not turn south to block the main army but comes here instead, he fears the Prince and despises me—

sentences.zh: 必不設備，可以計取之。」

translations.literal: He will certainly be unprepared, and we can take him by stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: he will surely be off guard, and we can take him by stratagem."

sentences.zh: 眾請治列人城，農曰：「善用兵者，結士以心，不以異物。

translations.literal: The officers asked to fortify the walls of Lieren; Nong said: "One who uses troops well binds men through the heart, not through external things.
translations.idiomatic: His officers asked to fortify Lieren, but Nong said: "A good commander binds his men by heart, not by walls.

sentences.zh: 今起義兵，唯敵是求，當以山河為城池，何列人之足治也！」

translations.literal: We have now raised a righteous army and seek only the enemy—we should take mountains and rivers as our walls; what need is there to fortify Lieren!"
translations.idiomatic: We have raised a righteous army to find the enemy. Let mountains and rivers be our walls—why bother fortifying Lieren!"

sentences.zh: 辛卯，越至列人西，農使趙秋及參軍綦毋滕擊越前鋒，破之。

translations.literal: On the day Xinmao, Yue reached west of Lieren; Nong sent Zhao Qiu and staff officer Qiwu Teng to strike Yue's vanguard and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Xinmao, Yue reached a point west of Lieren. Nong sent Zhao Qiu and staff officer Qiwu Teng against Yue's vanguard and broke it.

sentences.zh: 參軍太原趙謙言於農曰：「越甲仗雖精，人心危駭，易破也，宜急擊之。」

translations.literal: Staff officer Zhao Qian of Taiyuan said to Nong: "Yue's armor and weapons are fine, but his men's hearts are shaken and terrified—they will be easy to break; you should attack at once."
translations.idiomatic: Staff officer Zhao Qian of Taiyuan said to Nong: "Yue's arms are excellent, but his men are shaken and afraid. They will break easily. Strike now."

sentences.zh: 農曰：「彼甲在外，我甲在心，晝戰，則士卒見其外貌而憚之，不如待暮擊之，可以必克。」

translations.literal: Nong said: "Their armor is on the outside, ours is in the heart; if we fight by day the soldiers will see their outward appearance and fear them—it would be better to wait until evening to attack, and then we can be certain of victory."
translations.idiomatic: Nong said: "Their armor is on their bodies; ours is in our hearts. By day our men will see how formidable they look and lose nerve. Wait until evening, and victory is certain."

sentences.zh: 令軍士嚴備以待，毋得妄動。

translations.literal: He ordered the soldiers to stand ready in strict formation and not to stir recklessly.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his troops to hold themselves in strict readiness and not move without command.

sentences.zh: 越立柵自固，農笑謂諸將曰：「越兵精士眾，不乘其初至之銳以擊我，方更立柵，吾知其無能為也。」

translations.literal: Yue built palisades to fortify himself; Nong laughed and said to the generals: "Yue has elite troops and a numerous force, yet instead of using their fresh arrival to strike us he only builds palisades—I know he can accomplish nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Yue threw up palisades to secure his camp. Nong laughed and told his generals: "Yue has fine troops and great numbers, yet instead of using their first rush against us he only builds fences. I know he can do nothing."

sentences.zh: 向暮，農鼓噪出，陳於城西。

translations.literal: Toward evening Nong advanced with drums and clamor and formed battle lines west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk Nong marched out with drums and shouts and drew up his line west of the city.

sentences.zh: 牙門劉木請先攻越柵，農笑曰：「凡人見美食，誰不欲之，何得獨請！

translations.literal: Gate officer Liu Mu asked to attack Yue's palisade first; Nong laughed and said: "When anyone sees fine food, who does not want it—how can you ask for it alone!
translations.idiomatic: Gate officer Liu Mu asked to lead the assault on Yue's palisade. Nong laughed and said: "When anyone sees a feast, who does not want a share? Why should you ask alone!

sentences.zh: 然汝猛銳可嘉，當以先鋒惠汝。」

translations.literal: Yet your fierce valor is commendable; I shall favor you with the vanguard."
translations.idiomatic: Still, your boldness deserves praise. I will give you the vanguard."

sentences.zh: 木乃帥壯士四百騰柵而入，秦兵披靡；

translations.literal: Thereupon Mu led four hundred stalwarts, vaulted the palisade, and entered; the Qin soldiers broke and scattered;
translations.idiomatic: Mu then led four hundred picked men over the palisade and into the camp, and the Qin troops broke;

sentences.zh: 農督大眾隨之，大敗秦兵，斬越，送首於垂。

translations.literal: Nong led the main force after them, routed the Qin army, beheaded Yue, and sent his head to Chui.
translations.idiomatic: Nong brought up the main force behind him, routed the Qin army, killed Yue, and sent his head to Chui.

sentences.zh: 越與毛當，皆秦之驍將也，故秦王堅使助二子鎮守；

translations.literal: Both Yue and Mao Dang were fierce generals of Qin; therefore King Fu Jian of Qin had sent them to assist his two sons in holding the frontier;
translations.idiomatic: Both Yue and Mao Dang were among Qin's fiercest generals, which was why King Fu Jian had posted them to help his two sons hold the region;

sentences.zh: 既而相繼敗沒，人情騷動，所在盜賊群起。

translations.literal: Soon afterward they were defeated and killed in succession; public sentiment was shaken, and bandits rose in groups everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: When both were defeated and killed in turn, morale collapsed and bandits rose everywhere.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，燕王垂至鄴，改秦建元二十年為燕元年，服色朝儀，皆如舊章。

translations.literal: On the day Gengxu, Prince of Yan Murong Chui reached Ye, changed Qin's twentieth year of Jianyuan to the first year of Yan, and dress colors and court ceremonies all followed the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Gengxu, Murong Chui reached Ye. He changed Qin's twentieth year of Jianyuan to the first year of Yan and restored the old court dress and ritual.

sentences.zh: 以前岷山公庫辱官偉為左長史，肖尚書段崇為右長史，滎陽鄭豁等為從事中郎。

translations.literal: He appointed the former Duke of Minshan, Kuru Official Wei, as Left Chief Administrator; Master of Writing Duan Chong as Right Chief Administrator; and Zheng Huo of Xingyang and others as Attendant Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: He made the former Duke of Minshan, Kuru Official Wei, Left Chief Administrator; Master of Writing Duan Chong Right Chief Administrator; and Zheng Huo of Xingyang and others Attendant Gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 慕容農引兵會垂於鄴，垂因其所稱之官而授之。

translations.literal: Murong Nong led his troops to join Chui at Ye; Chui conferred on him the offices he had already assumed.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Nong brought his army to join Chui at Ye, and Chui confirmed the titles Nong had already taken upon himself.

sentences.zh: 立世子寶為太子，封從弟拔等十七人及甥宇文輸、舅子蘭審皆為王；

translations.literal: He established heir apparent Bao as crown prince, enfeoffed seventeen younger cousins including Ba and others as princes, as well as his nephew by marriage Yuwen Shu and his maternal nephew's son Lan Shen—all as kings;
translations.idiomatic: He made heir apparent Bao crown prince and enfeoffed seventeen younger cousins including Ba, his nephew by marriage Yuwen Shu, and his maternal nephew's son Lan Shen—all as kings;

sentences.zh: 其餘宗族及功臣封公者三十七人，侯、伯、子，男者八十九人。

translations.literal: Among the rest of the clansmen and meritorious officials, thirty-seven were enfeoffed as dukes; eighty-nine as marquises, counts, viscounts, or barons.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-seven other clansmen and meritorious officials were made dukes, and eighty-nine more were made marquises, counts, viscounts, or barons.

sentences.zh: 可足渾潭集兵得二萬餘人，攻野王，拔之，引兵會攻鄴。

translations.literal: Kezuhun Tan gathered more than twenty thousand troops, attacked Yewang, captured it, and led his army to join the siege of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Kezuhun Tan raised more than twenty thousand men, took Yewang, and marched to join the siege of Ye.

sentences.zh: 平幼及弟睿、規亦帥眾數萬會垂於鄴。

translations.literal: Ping You and his brothers Rui and Gui also led tens of thousands to join Chui at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Ping You and his brothers Rui and Gui also brought tens of thousands of men to join Chui at Ye.

sentences.zh: 長樂公丕使姜讓誚讓燕王垂，且說之曰：「過而能改，今猶未晚也。」

translations.literal: The Duke of Changle, Fu Pi, sent Jiang Rang to reprove Prince of Yan Murong Chui and also said to him: "If one can amend after a fault, it is still not too late."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi, Duke of Changle, sent Jiang Rang to rebuke Murong Chui and also told him: "It is not too late to turn back from error."

sentences.zh: 垂曰：「孤受主上不世之恩，故欲安全長樂公，使盡眾赴京師，然後修復國家之業，與秦永為鄰好。

translations.literal: Chui said: "I have received unexampled favor from the sovereign, and therefore wish to ensure the Duke of Changle's safety—let him bring all his forces to the capital—then I will restore the national enterprise and remain forever neighbor and ally with Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Chui said: "I owe the sovereign a debt beyond measure, which is why I wish to see the Duke of Changle safe—let him bring all his forces to the capital—then I will restore our realm and keep eternal peace with Qin.

sentences.zh: 何故暗於機運，不以鄴城見歸？

translations.literal: Why are you blind to the tide of fortune and unwilling to surrender Ye?
translations.idiomatic: Why do you fail to read the times and refuse to hand over Ye?

sentences.zh: 若迷而不復，當窮極兵勢，恐單馬求生，亦不可得也。」

translations.literal: If you persist in error and do not turn back, I shall exhaust every measure of force; I fear that even seeking life on a single horse will then be impossible."
translations.idiomatic: If you persist in your mistake, I will bring every force I have to bear, and I doubt you will even escape alive on a single horse."

sentences.zh: 讓厲色責之曰：「將軍不容於家國，投命聖朝，燕之尺土，將軍豈有分乎？

translations.literal: Rang said sternly in rebuke: "The general found no place in his own state and cast his lot with the sacred dynasty—did the general ever have any share in a single foot of Yan's soil?
translations.idiomatic: Rang said sharply: "You found no place in your own realm and cast your lot with the sacred dynasty. Did you ever own a single foot of Yan's soil?

sentences.zh: 主上與將軍風殊類別，一見傾心，親如宗戚，寵逾勳舊，自古君臣際遇，有如是之厚者乎？

translations.literal: The sovereign and the general differ in custom and kind; at first meeting hearts were joined, intimacy like that of kinsmen, favor surpassing the meritorious veterans—since ancient times has there ever been such thickness in the meeting of lord and minister?
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign and you differ in custom and race, yet at first sight he gave you his heart, treated you like kin, and favored you above old merit—when in all history has a lord shown a minister such devotion?

sentences.zh: 一旦因王師小敗，遽有異圖。

translations.literal: Yet at a single small defeat of the royal army you suddenly harbor a separate design.
translations.idiomatic: Yet after one small defeat of the imperial army you suddenly turn traitor.

sentences.zh: 長樂公，主上元子，受分陝之任，寧可束手輸將軍以百城之地乎？

translations.literal: The Duke of Changle is the sovereign's eldest son and bears the charge of dividing Shan—could he meekly hand over a hundred cities' worth of territory to the general?
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Changle is the sovereign's eldest son and holds the charge of guarding the western frontier. Would he meekly surrender a hundred cities to you?

sentences.zh: 將軍欲裂冠毀冕，自可極其兵勢，奚更云云！

translations.literal: If the general wishes to tear cap and destroy crown, he may by all means exert his military power to the limit—why further idle words!
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to tear the crown from your head and play rebel, then by all means bring all your force to bear—why waste words!

sentences.zh: 但惜將軍以七十之年，懸首白旗，高世之忠，更為逆鬼耳！」

translations.literal: Only it is a pity that the general, at seventy years, should hang his head from a white banner—the loyalty that would have elevated him above his age will instead make him a rebel ghost!"
translations.idiomatic: Only it is a pity that a man of seventy should end with his head on a white pole—the loyalty that might have made you immortal will instead make you a rebel ghost!"

sentences.zh: 垂默然。

translations.literal: Chui was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Chui said nothing.

sentences.zh: 左右請殺之，垂曰：「彼各為其主耳，何罪！」

translations.literal: Those at his side asked to kill him; Chui said: "He serves his own lord—what crime is that!
translations.idiomatic: Those around him asked to kill Rang, but Chui said: "He serves his own master. What crime is that!

sentences.zh: 禮而歸之，遺丕書及上秦王堅表，陳述利害，請送丕歸長安。

translations.literal: He treated him with courtesy and sent him back, wrote to Pi and submitted a memorial to King Fu Jian of Qin, setting forth advantage and harm and asking that Pi be sent back to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He treated him with courtesy and sent him back, then wrote to Pi and submitted a memorial to King Fu Jian of Qin explaining the stakes and asking that Pi be allowed to return to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 堅及丕怒，復書切責之。

translations.literal: Fu Jian and Fu Pi were enraged and replied with a letter of bitter rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian and Fu Pi were furious and answered with a letter of sharp rebuke.

sentences.zh: 鷹揚將軍劉牢之攻秦譙城，拔之。

translations.literal: Striking Eagle General Liu Laozhi attacked Qiao city of Qin and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Striking Eagle General Liu Laozhi attacked Qiao in Qin territory and took it.

sentences.zh: 桓沖遣上庸太守郭寶攻秦魏興、上庸、新城三郡，拔之。

translations.literal: Huan Chong sent Governor of Shangyong Guo Bao to attack the three commanderies of Weixing, Shangyong, and Xincheng under Qin and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Chong sent Guo Bao, governor of Shangyong, to attack the Qin commanderies of Weixing, Shangyong, and Xincheng, and all three fell.

sentences.zh: 將軍楊佺期進據成固，擊秦梁州刺史潘猛，走之。

translations.literal: General Yang Quanqi advanced and seized Chenggu, attacked Qin Governor of Liangzhou Pan Meng, and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: General Yang Quanqi advanced, seized Chenggu, and attacked Qin's governor of Liangzhou, Pan Meng, driving him back.

sentences.zh: 佺期，亮之子也。

translations.literal: Quanqi was Liang's son.
translations.idiomatic: Quanqi was the son of Yang Liang.

sentences.zh: 壬子，燕王垂攻鄴，拔其外郭，長樂公丕退守中城。

translations.literal: On the day Renzi, Prince of Yan Murong Chui attacked Ye, captured its outer wall; the Duke of Changle Fu Pi withdrew to hold the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Renzi, Murong Chui attacked Ye and took the outer walls; Fu Pi, Duke of Changle, withdrew to the inner citadel.

sentences.zh: 關東六州郡縣多送任請降於燕。

translations.literal: Many commanderies and counties of the six eastern provinces sent hostages and requested surrender to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Many commanderies and counties east of the pass sent hostages and offered to surrender to Yan.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，垂以陳留王紹行冀州刺史，屯廣阿。

translations.literal: On the day Guichou, Chui made Prince of Chenliu Shao acting Governor of Jizhou and encamped at Guanga.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Guichou, Chui appointed Prince of Chenliu Shao acting governor of Jizhou and posted him at Guanga.

sentences.zh: 豐城宣穆公桓沖聞謝玄等有功，自以失言，慚恨成疾；

translations.literal: Duke Xuanmu of Fengcheng, Huan Chong, heard that Xie Xuan and others had achieved merit; thinking he had spoken wrongly, shame and resentment became illness;
translations.idiomatic: Huan Chong, Duke Xuanmu of Fengcheng, heard of the victories of Xie Xuan and the others; ashamed that he had spoken too hastily, he fell ill from regret;

sentences.zh: 二月，辛巳，卒。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day Xinsi, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day Xinsi, he died.

sentences.zh: 朝議欲以謝玄為荊、江二州刺史。

translations.literal: At court it was proposed to make Xie Xuan Governor of both Jing and Jiang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The court discussed appointing Xie Xuan governor of both Jing and Jiang provinces.

sentences.zh: 謝安自以父子名位太盛，又懼桓氏失職怨望，乃以梁郡太守桓石民為荊州刺史，河東太守桓石虔為豫州刺史，豫州刺史桓伊為江州刺史。

translations.literal: Xie An, considering that father and son held too lofty names and positions, and fearing that the Huan clan, deprived of office, would harbor resentment, therefore made Liangjun Prefect Huan Shimin Governor of Jingzhou, Hedong Prefect Huan Shiqian Governor of Yuzhou, and Governor of Yuzhou Huan Yi Governor of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An, fearing that he and his son had risen too high and that the Huans, displaced from office, would turn resentful, made Huan Shimin, prefect of Liangjun, governor of Jingzhou; Huan Shiqian, prefect of Hedong, governor of Yuzhou; and Huan Yi, already governor of Yuzhou, governor of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 燕王垂引丁零、烏桓之眾二十餘萬為飛梯地道以攻鄴，不拔；

translations.literal: Prince of Yan Murong Chui led more than two hundred thousand Dingling and Wuhuan troops, building flying ladders and underground tunnels to attack Ye, but did not capture it;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui brought more than two hundred thousand Dingling and Wuhuan warriors, using siege towers and sappers to assault Ye, but could not take the city;

sentences.zh: 乃築長圍守之，分處老弱於肥鄉，築新興城以置輜重。

translations.literal: Then he built a long encirclement to besiege it, distributed the old and weak at Feixiang, and built Xinxing city to store baggage trains.
translations.idiomatic: He then settled in for a long siege, sent the elderly and weak to Feixiang, and built Xinxing city to store his supplies.

sentences.zh: 秦征東府官屬疑參軍高泰，燕之舊臣，有貳心。

translations.literal: The staff of Qin's Eastern Expedition headquarters suspected Attendant Gentleman Gao Tai, an old minister of Yan, of divided loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The staff of Qin's eastern expedition command suspected Gao Tai, a former Yan official serving as an attendant gentleman, of disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 泰懼，與同郡虞曹從事吳韶逃歸勃海。

translations.literal: Tai feared this and, with Wu Shao of the same commandery, a clerk in the Bureau of Parks, fled back to Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: In fear, Gao Tai fled to Bohai with Wu Shao, a clerk in the Bureau of Parks from his home commandery.

sentences.zh: 韶曰：「燕軍近在肥鄉，宜從之。」

translations.literal: Shao said: "The Yan army is near at Feixiang—we ought to join them."
translations.idiomatic: Shao said: "The Yan army is close by at Feixiang. We ought to go over to them."

sentences.zh: 泰曰：「吾以避禍耳；

translations.literal: Tai said: "I am only trying to escape disaster;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Tai replied: "I am only trying to escape harm;

sentences.zh: 去一君，事一君，吾所不為也！」

translations.literal: to leave one lord and serve another—that I will not do!"
translations.idiomatic: to leave one master and serve another is something I will not do!"

sentences.zh: 申紹見而歎曰：「去就以道，可謂君子矣！」

translations.literal: Shen Shao saw this and sighed: "In choosing to go or stay according to principle—one may call him a gentleman!"
translations.idiomatic: Shen Shao witnessed this and sighed: "Choosing to go or stay according to principle—here is a true gentleman!"

sentences.zh: 燕范陽王德擊秦枋頭，取之，置戍而還。

translations.literal: Prince of Fanyang of Yan, Murong De, attacked Qin's Fangtou, captured it, set a garrison, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De, Prince of Fanyang, attacked Fangtou, took it, left a garrison, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 東胡王晏據館陶，為鄴中聲援，鮮卑、烏桓及郡縣民據塢壁不從燕者尚眾；

translations.literal: Eastern Hu king Yan held Guantao as a support for Ye; Xianbei, Wuhuan, and people of commanderies and counties holding fortified walls who would not submit to Yan were still numerous;
translations.idiomatic: Yan, king of the Eastern Hu, held Guantao to support Ye; many Xianbei, Wuhuan, and local people still held out in fortified stockades and refused to submit to Yan;

sentences.zh: 燕王垂遣太原王楷與鎮南將軍陳留王紹討之。

translations.literal: Prince of Yan Murong Chui sent Prince of Taiyuan Kai and Pacify-the-South General Prince of Chenliu Shao to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui sent Prince of Taiyuan Kai and Pacify-the-South General Prince of Chenliu Shao to subdue them.

sentences.zh: 楷謂紹曰：「鮮卑、烏桓及冀州之民，本皆燕臣。

translations.literal: Kai said to Shao: "The Xianbei, Wuhuan, and people of Jizhou were all originally Yan's subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Kai told Shao: "The Xianbei, Wuhuan, and the people of Jizhou were all once Yan's subjects.

sentences.zh: 今大業始爾，人心未洽，所以小異。

translations.literal: Now the great enterprise has only just begun and hearts are not yet reconciled—that is why there is slight dissent.
translations.idiomatic: Our cause has only just begun, and hearts are not yet won—that is why they hold back.

sentences.zh: 唯宜綏之以德，不可震之以威。

translations.literal: One should only soothe them with virtue and must not awe them with force.
translations.idiomatic: We must win them with kindness, not intimidate them with force.

sentences.zh: 吾當止一處，為軍聲之本，汝巡撫民夷，示以大義，彼必當聽從。」

translations.literal: I shall stay at one place as the army's base of authority; you patrol among the people and tribes, showing them the greater principle—they will surely obey."
translations.idiomatic: I will hold one position as the anchor of our army; you go among the people and tribes, show them the right cause, and they will surely come over."

sentences.zh: 楷乃屯於辟陽。

translations.literal: Kai then encamped at Piyang.
translations.idiomatic: Kai then encamped at Piyang.

sentences.zh: 紹帥騎數百往說王晏，為陳禍福，晏隨紹詣楷降，於是鮮卑、烏桓及塢民降者數十萬口。

translations.literal: Shao led several hundred horsemen to persuade King Yan, setting forth fortune and disaster; Yan followed Shao to Kai to surrender, whereupon Xianbei, Wuhuan, and stockade people who surrendered numbered several hundred thousand mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Shao rode out with a few hundred cavalry to persuade King Yan, explaining the stakes; Yan went with Shao to Kai and submitted, and in the end several hundred thousand Xianbei, Wuhuan, and stockade dwellers surrendered.

sentences.zh: 楷留其老弱，置守宰以撫之，發其丁壯十餘萬，與王晏詣鄴。

translations.literal: Kai kept their old and weak, set guards and officials to soothe them, and dispatched more than one hundred thousand of their able-bodied men, together with King Yan, to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Kai left the elderly and weak behind with local officials to settle them, drafted more than one hundred thousand able-bodied men, and went with King Yan to Ye.

sentences.zh: 垂大悅，曰：「汝兄弟才兼文武，足以繼先王矣！」

translations.literal: Chui was greatly pleased and said: "You brothers combine civil and military talent—enough to succeed the former king!"
translations.idiomatic: Chui was delighted and said: "You brothers possess both civil and military talent—you are fit to carry on the work of our forefathers!"

sentences.zh: 三月，以衛將軍謝安為太保。

translations.literal: In the third month, Guard General Xie An was made Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Xie An was appointed grand mentor.

sentences.zh: 秦北地長史慕容泓聞燕王垂攻鄴，亡奔關東，收集鮮卑，眾至數千。

translations.literal: Qin's Chief Administrator of Beidi, Murong Hong, hearing that Prince of Yan Murong Chui was attacking Ye, fled east of the pass, gathered Xianbei, and his force reached several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hong, chief administrator of Beidi under Qin, heard that Murong Chui was attacking Ye; he fled east of the pass, rallied the Xianbei, and raised several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 還屯華陰，敗秦將軍強永，其眾遂盛。

translations.literal: He returned and encamped at Huayin, defeated Qin General Qiang Yong, and his force then flourished.
translations.idiomatic: He returned and encamped at Huayin, defeated Qin general Qiang Yong, and his following grew strong.

sentences.zh: 自稱都督陝西諸軍事、大將軍、雍州牧、濟北王，推垂為丞相、都督陝東諸軍事、領大司馬、冀州牧、吳王。

translations.literal: He styled himself Grand Commander of All Military Affairs in Shaanxi, Grand General, Governor of Yongzhou, and Prince of Jibei, and promoted Chui as Chancellor, Grand Commander of All Military Affairs in Shandong, concurrently Grand Commandant, Governor of Jizhou, and Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed himself grand commander of all military affairs west of the mountain passes, grand general, governor of Yongzhou, and Prince of Jibei, and hailed Chui as chancellor, grand commander east of the passes, grand commandant, governor of Jizhou, and Prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅謂權翼曰：「不用卿言，使鮮卑至此。

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin said to Quan Yi: "By not heeding your words I have brought the Xianbei to this.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian said to Quan Yi: "Because I did not heed your advice, the Xianbei have come to this.

sentences.zh: 關東之地，吾不復與之爭，將若泓何？」

translations.literal: The lands east of the pass—I will no longer contend for them with them. What shall we do about Hong?"
translations.idiomatic: I will no longer fight them for the lands east of the pass. What are we to do about Hong?"

sentences.zh: 乃以廣平公熙為雍州刺史，鎮蒲阪。

translations.literal: He then made Duke of Guangping Xi Governor of Yongzhou, garrisoning Puban.
translations.idiomatic: He then made Duke of Guangping Xi governor of Yongzhou and posted him at Puban.

sentences.zh: 征雍州牧巨鹿公睿為都督中外諸軍事、衛大將軍、錄尚書事，配兵五萬；

translations.literal: He summoned Governor of Yongzhou Duke Min of Julu Rui to be Grand Commander of All Internal and External Military Affairs, Guard Grand General, and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing affairs, assigning him fifty thousand troops;
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Duke Min of Julu Rui, governor of Yongzhou, to serve as supreme commander of all forces, guard grand general, and supervisor of the Masters of Writing, with fifty thousand men;

sentences.zh: 以左將軍竇沖為長史，龍驤將軍姚萇為司馬，以討泓。

translations.literal: he made Left General Dou Chong Chief Administrator and Flying Dragon General Yao Chang Staff Officer, to attack Hong.
translations.idiomatic: and appointed Left General Dou Chong chief administrator and Flying Dragon General Yao Chang staff officer to campaign against Hong.

sentences.zh: 平陽太守慕容沖亦起兵於平陽，有眾二萬，進攻蒲阪；

translations.literal: Administrator of Pingyang Murong Chong also raised troops at Pingyang, with a force of twenty thousand, and advanced to attack Puban;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chong, administrator of Pingyang, also rose in rebellion there with twenty thousand men and marched on Puban;

sentences.zh: 堅使竇沖討之。

translations.literal: Fu Jian sent Dou Chong to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian sent Dou Chong against him.

sentences.zh: 庫辱官偉帥營部數萬至鄴，燕王垂封偉為安定王。

translations.literal: Kuru Official Wei led several tens of thousands of camp followers to Ye; Prince of Yan Murong Chui enfeoffed Wei as Prince of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Kuru Official Wei led tens of thousands of camp followers to Ye, and Murong Chui enfeoffed him as Prince of Anding.

sentences.zh: 秦冀州刺史阜城侯定守信都，高城男紹在其國，高邑侯亮、重合侯謨守常山，固安侯鑒守中山。

translations.literal: Qin Governor of Jizhou Marquis of Fucheng Fu Ding held Xindu; Baron of Gaocheng Shao was in his domain; Marquis of Gaoyi Fu Liang and Marquis of Chonghe Fu Mo held Changshan; Marquis of Gu'an Fu Jian held Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Ding, Marquis of Fucheng and Qin governor of Jizhou, held Xindu; Baron of Gaocheng Shao was within his territory; Fu Liang, Marquis of Gaoyi, and Fu Mo, Marquis of Chonghe, held Changshan; Fu Jian, Marquis of Gu'an, held Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 燕王垂遣前將軍、樂浪王溫督諸軍攻信都，不克；

translations.literal: Prince of Yan Murong Chui sent Forward General Prince of Lelang Wen to command the armies in attacking Xindu, but did not capture it;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui sent Forward General Prince of Lelang Wen to lead the assault on Xindu, but the city held;

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙辰，遣撫軍大將軍麟益兵助之。

translations.literal: in summer, the fourth month, on the day Bingchen, he sent Pacification Grand General Lin with reinforcements to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: in the fourth month of summer, on the day Bingchen, he sent Pacification Grand General Lin with reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 定、鑒，秦王堅之從叔；

translations.literal: Fu Ding and Marquis Fu Jian were paternal uncles of King Fu Jian of Qin;
translations.idiomatic: Fu Ding and the Marquis of Gu'an were Fu Jian's paternal uncles;

sentences.zh: 紹、謨，從弟；

translations.literal: Shao and Mo were younger cousins;
translations.idiomatic: Shao and Mo were younger cousins of his;

sentences.zh: 亮，從子也。

translations.literal: Liang was a cousin's son.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was a nephew.

sentences.zh: 溫，燕王垂之弟子也。

translations.literal: Wen was a younger cousin's son of Prince of Yan Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: Wen was Murong Chui's nephew.

sentences.zh: 慕容泓聞秦兵且至，懼，帥眾將奔關東。

translations.literal: Murong Hong, hearing that Qin troops were about to arrive, was afraid and led his force intending to flee east of the pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Hong learned that Qin troops were approaching, he panicked and prepared to flee east of the pass with his army.

sentences.zh: 秦巨鹿愍公睿粗猛輕敵，欲馳兵邀之。

translations.literal: Qin's Duke Min of Julu Rui was coarse, fierce, and contemptuous of the enemy; he wished to gallop his troops to intercept them.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Min of Julu Rui was rash and overconfident; he wanted to ride out and cut Hong off.

sentences.zh: 姚萇諫曰：「鮮卑皆有思歸之志，故起而為亂，宜驅令出關，不可遏也。

translations.literal: Yao Chang remonstrated: "The Xianbei all harbor a desire to return home—that is why they rose in revolt; they should be driven to leave the pass and must not be blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang urged: "The Xianbei are rebelling because they long to go home. We should drive them out of the pass, not try to stop them.

sentences.zh: 夫執鼷鼠之尾，猶能反噬於人。

translations.literal: For if you grasp even a field mouse by the tail, it can still turn and bite a man.
translations.idiomatic: Even a cornered field mouse will bite.

sentences.zh: 彼自知困窮，致死於我；

translations.literal: They, knowing they are trapped and desperate, will fight us to the death;
translations.idiomatic: Cornered and desperate, they will fight to the death;

sentences.zh: 萬一失利，悔將何及！

translations.literal: if by any chance we fail, what regret will there be time for!
translations.idiomatic: if we suffer even one setback, it will be too late for regret!

sentences.zh: 但可鳴鼓隨之，彼將奔敗不暇矣。」

translations.literal: One need only beat drums and follow them—they will flee in defeat with no time to spare."
translations.idiomatic: Just beat the drums and pursue—they will scatter in flight and never look back."

sentences.zh: 睿弗從，戰於華澤，睿兵敗，為泓所殺。

translations.literal: Rui did not agree; they fought at Huaze; Rui's army was defeated and he was killed by Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Rui refused to listen. At Huaze his army was routed and Hong killed him.

sentences.zh: 萇遣龍驤長史趙都、參軍姜協詣秦王堅謝罪；

translations.literal: Chang sent Flying Dragon Chief Administrator Zhao Du and Attendant Gentleman Jiang Xie to King Fu Jian of Qin to apologize;
translations.idiomatic: Chang sent his chief administrator Zhao Du and attendant gentleman Jiang Xie to Fu Jian to apologize;

sentences.zh: 堅怒，殺之。

translations.literal: Fu Jian was enraged and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian, furious, had them executed.

sentences.zh: 萇懼，奔渭北馬牧。

translations.literal: Chang feared this and fled to the horse pastures north of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In fear, Chang fled to the horse pastures north of the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 於是天水尹緯、尹詳、南龐演等糾扇羌豪，帥其戶口歸萇者五萬餘家，推萇為盟主。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yin Wei of Tianshui, Yin Xiang, Pang Yan of Nan, and others rallied Qiang chieftains; households that followed Chang numbered more than fifty thousand families, and they made Chang their alliance leader.
translations.idiomatic: Then Yin Wei and Yin Xiang of Tianshui, Pang Yan of Nan, and others rallied Qiang chieftains; more than fifty thousand households came over to Chang and proclaimed him their leader.

sentences.zh: 萇自稱大將軍、大單于、萬年秦王，大赦，改元白雀，以尹詳、龐演為左、右長史，南安姚晃及尹緯為左、右司馬，天水狄伯支等為從事中郎，羌訓等為掾屬，王據等為參軍，王欽盧、姚方成等為將帥。

translations.literal: Chang styled himself Grand General, Grand Chanyu, and King of Qin of Wannian; proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to White Sparrow; made Yin Xiang and Pang Yan Left and Right Chief Administrators; Nanan Yao Huang and Yin Wei Left and Right Staff Officers; Tianshui Di Bozhi and others Attendant Gentlemen; Qiang Xun and others clerical aides; Wang Ju and others staff advisers; Wang Qinlu, Yao Fangcheng, and others generals.
translations.idiomatic: Chang proclaimed himself grand general, grand chanyu, and King of Qin of Wannian; declared a general amnesty and adopted the era name White Sparrow. He made Yin Xiang and Pang Yan left and right chief administrators; Yao Huang of Nanan and Yin Wei left and right staff officers; Di Bozhi of Tianshui and others attendant gentlemen; Qiang Xun and others clerks; Wang Ju and others staff advisers; and Wang Qinlu, Yao Fangcheng, and others his commanders.

sentences.zh: 秦竇衝擊慕容沖於河東，大破之；

translations.literal: Qin's Dou Chong attacked Murong Chong at Hedong and routed him greatly;
translations.idiomatic: Dou Chong of Qin attacked Murong Chong in Hedong and routed him;

sentences.zh: 沖帥鮮卑騎八千奔慕容泓。

translations.literal: Chong led eight thousand Xianbei cavalry to flee to Murong Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Chong fled with eight thousand Xianbei horsemen to join Murong Hong.

sentences.zh: 泓眾至十餘萬，遣使謂秦王堅曰：「吳王已定關東，可速資備大駕，奉送家兄皇帝，泓當帥關中燕人翼衛乘輿，還返鄴都，與秦以虎牢為界，永為鄰好。」

translations.literal: Hong's force reached more than one hundred thousand; he sent envoys to tell King Fu Jian of Qin: "The Prince of Wu has already settled the east of the pass—quickly prepare the imperial equipage and send my elder brother the emperor; Hong will lead the Yan people of Guanzhong to escort the imperial carriage, return to the capital at Ye, take Hulao as the boundary with Qin, and be neighbors in perpetual amity."
translations.idiomatic: Hong's army swelled to more than one hundred thousand. He sent envoys to Fu Jian: "The Prince of Wu has secured the east. Prepare the imperial train at once and send my brother the emperor. I will lead the Yan people of Guanzhong to escort him back to Ye. Let Hulao mark the border between us, and let us live as neighbors in peace forever."

sentences.zh: 堅大怒，召慕容□責之曰：「今泓書如此，卿欲去者，朕當相資。

translations.literal: Fu Jian was greatly enraged, summoned Murong Wei and rebuked him: "Now Hong's letter reads thus—if you wish to go, I shall supply you.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian flew into a rage and summoned Murong Wei. "Hong writes this to me. If you wish to leave, I will furnish you for the journey.

sentences.zh: 卿之宗族，可謂人面獸心，不可以國士期也！」

translations.literal: Your clan—one may say human faces with beast hearts; they cannot be treated as men fit for national service!"
translations.idiomatic: Your clan has human faces and beasts' hearts—they are not men one can honor as true subjects of the realm!"

sentences.zh: □叩頭流血，涕泣陳謝。

translations.literal: Murong Wei knocked his head until it bled, weeping as he pleaded forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Wei knocked his forehead until it bled, weeping as he pleaded for mercy.

sentences.zh: 堅久之曰：「此自三豎所為，非卿之過。」

translations.literal: After a long while Fu Jian said: "This is what those three wretches have done—not your fault."
translations.idiomatic: After a long silence Fu Jian said: "This is the work of those three upstarts, not yours."

sentences.zh: 復其位，待之如初。

translations.literal: He restored him to his position and treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: He restored Murong Wei to his post and treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 命□以書招諭泓、沖及垂。

translations.literal: He ordered Murong Wei to write letters summoning and persuading Hong, Chong, and Chui.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Murong Wei to write letters summoning Hong, Chong, and Chui to submit.

sentences.zh: □密遣使謂泓曰：「吾籠中之人，必無還理；

translations.literal: Murong Wei secretly sent envoys to tell Hong: "I am a man in a cage—there is surely no prospect of return;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Wei secretly sent word to Hong: "I am a prisoner here. I shall never return;

sentences.zh: 且燕室之罪人也，不足復顧。

translations.literal: moreover I am a guilty man of the house of Yan—not worth troubling over further.
translations.idiomatic: and I am already a criminal of the house of Yan—not worth thinking of again.

sentences.zh: 汝勉建大業，以吳王為相國，中山王為太宰、領大司馬，汝可為大將軍、領司徒，承製封拜，聽吾死問，汝便即尊位。」

translations.literal: You strive to establish the great enterprise: make the Prince of Wu chancellor; the Prince of Zhongshan Grand Mentor and concurrently Grand Commandant; you may be Grand General and concurrently Minister of Works; receive imperial edicts to enfeoff and appoint; when you hear of my death, you may then immediately assume the throne."
translations.idiomatic: Press on with the great cause. Make the Prince of Wu your chancellor, the Prince of Zhongshan grand mentor and grand commandant, and take for yourself the titles of grand general and minister of works. Issue appointments by edict as you see fit, and when you receive word of my death, take the throne at once."

sentences.zh: 泓於是進向長安，改元燕興。

translations.literal: Hong thereupon advanced toward Chang'an and changed the era name to Yanxing.
translations.idiomatic: Hong then marched on Chang'an and adopted the era name Yanxing.

sentences.zh: 燕王垂以鄴城猶固，會僚佐議之。

translations.literal: Prince of Yan Murong Chui, because Ye city was still firm, gathered his staff to deliberate on it.
translations.idiomatic: Because Ye still held out, Murong Chui assembled his advisers to discuss what to do.

sentences.zh: 右司馬封衡請引漳水灌之；

translations.literal: Right Staff Officer Feng Heng asked to divert the waters of the Zhang to flood it;
translations.idiomatic: Right staff officer Feng Heng proposed flooding the city with the Zhang River;

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Chui agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Chui agreed.

sentences.zh: 垂行圍，因飲於華林園，秦人密出兵掩之，矢下如雨，垂幾不得出，冠軍大將軍隆將騎沖之，垂僅而得免。

translations.literal: Chui went on a tour of the encirclement and, while drinking in Huaglin Garden, Qin men secretly sent troops to surprise them; arrows fell like rain; Chui nearly could not escape; Champion Grand General Long led cavalry to charge through and Chui barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Chui toured the siege lines and took refreshment in Huaglin Garden. Qin troops launched a surprise attack; arrows fell like rain and Chui nearly failed to escape. Champion grand general Murong Long charged in with cavalry and Chui barely got away.

sentences.zh: 竟陵太守趙統攻襄陽，秦荊州刺史都貴奔魯陽。

translations.literal: Administrator of Jingling Zhao Tong attacked Xiangyang; Qin Governor of Jingzhou Du Gui fled to Luyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tong, administrator of Jingling, attacked Xiangyang; Du Gui, Qin's governor of Jingzhou, fled to Luyang.

sentences.zh: 五月，秦洛州刺史張五虎據豐陽來降。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Qin Governor of Luozhou Zhang Wuhu, holding Fengyang, came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Zhang Wuhu, Qin's governor of Luozhou, holding Fengyang, surrendered.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史楊亮帥眾五萬伐蜀，遣巴西太守費統等將水陸兵三萬為前鋒。

translations.literal: Governor of Liangzhou Yang Liang led a force of fifty thousand to attack Shu, sending Administrator of Baxi Fei Tong and others to command thirty thousand water and land troops as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Liang, governor of Liangzhou, led fifty thousand men against Shu and sent Fei Tong, administrator of Baxi, and others with thirty thousand land and river troops as the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 亮屯巴郡，秦益州刺史王廣遣巴西太守康回等拒之。

translations.literal: Liang encamped at Bajun; Qin Governor of Yizhou Wang Guang sent Administrator of Baxi Kang Hui and others to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang encamped in Baxi; Wang Guang, Qin's governor of Yizhou, sent Kang Hui, administrator of Baxi, and others to resist him.

sentences.zh: 秦苻定、苻紹皆降於燕，燕慕容麟引兵西攻常山。

translations.literal: Qin's Fu Ding and Fu Shao both surrendered to Yan; Murong Lin of Yan led troops west to attack Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Ding and Fu Shao of Qin surrendered to Yan, and Murong Lin marched west against Changshan.

sentences.zh: 後秦王萇進屯北地，秦華陰、北地、新平、安定羌胡降之者十餘萬。

translations.literal: Later King of Qin Yao Chang advanced and encamped at Beidi; Qiang and Hu of Huayin, Beidi, Xiping, and Anding who submitted to him numbered more than one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Later King Yao Chang advanced into Beidi, and more than one hundred thousand Qiang and tribal peoples from Huayin, Beidi, Xiping, and Anding submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 六月，癸丑朔，崇德太后褚氏崩。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the first day of the month, Gui-chou, Empress Dowager Chongde of the Chu clan died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the first day Gui-chou, Empress Dowager Chongde, née Chu, died.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅自帥步騎二萬以擊後秦，軍於趙氏塢，使護軍將軍楊璧等分道攻之；

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin personally led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Later Qin, encamping at the Zhao clan's stockade, and sent Guard-the-Army General Yang Bi and others to attack by separate routes;
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian personally led twenty thousand foot and horse to attack Later Qin, encamping at Zhao's stockade, and sent Guard-the-Army General Yang Bi and others against him on several axes;

sentences.zh: 後秦兵屢敗，斬後秦王萇之弟鎮軍將軍尹買。

translations.literal: Later Qin troops were repeatedly defeated; Guard-the-Army General Yin Mai, younger brother of Later King of Qin Yao Chang, was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qin suffered repeated defeats, and Yao Chang's younger brother Yin Mai, guard-the-army general, was killed.

sentences.zh: 後秦軍中無井，秦人塞安公谷、堰同官水以固之。

translations.literal: Later Qin army had no wells; Qin men blocked Angong Valley and dammed Tongguan water to secure this.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Qin camp had no wells; the Qin forces blocked Angong Valley and dammed the Tongguan River to cut off their water.

sentences.zh: 後秦人恟懼，有渴死者。

translations.literal: The people of Later Qin were frightened and alarmed; some died of thirst.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qin's men panicked, and some died of thirst.

sentences.zh: 會天大雨，後秦營中水三尺，繞營百步之外，寸餘而已，後秦軍復振。

translations.literal: It happened that heaven sent great rain; within Later Qin's camp water was three feet deep, while beyond a hundred paces around the camp there was barely an inch, and Later Qin's army revived.
translations.idiomatic: Then heaven sent a downpour. Three feet of water pooled in the Later Qin camp, while barely an inch fell a hundred paces beyond their lines, and their army rallied.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅歎曰：「天亦佑賊乎！」

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin sighed: "Does heaven also protect rebels!"
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian sighed: "Does heaven favor these rebels after all!"

sentences.zh: 慕容泓謀臣高蓋等以泓德望不如慕容沖，且持法苛峻，乃殺泓，立沖為皇太弟，承製行事，置百官；

translations.literal: Hong's plotting ministers Gao Gai and others, because Hong's virtue and standing did not equal Murong Chong's and because he enforced the law with harsh severity, thereupon killed Hong, installed Chong as imperial younger brother-heir, acted by received edict, and established the hundred officials;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gai and other advisers, finding Hong's prestige inferior to Murong Chong's and his justice too harsh, killed Hong and made Chong imperial younger brother-heir, governing by edict and establishing a full bureaucracy;

sentences.zh: 以蓋為尚書令。

translations.literal: they made Gai Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gai was made minister of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 後秦王萇遣其子嵩為質於沖以請和。

translations.literal: Later King of Qin Yao Chang sent his son Song as hostage to Chong to sue for peace.
translations.idiomatic: Later King Yao Chang sent his son Song as a hostage to Chong to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 將軍劉春攻魯陽，都貴奔還長安。

translations.literal: General Liu Chun attacked Luyang; Du Gui fled back to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: General Liu Chun attacked Luyang, and Du Gui fled back to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 後秦王萇帥眾七萬擊秦，秦王堅遣楊璧等拒之，為萇所敗；

translations.literal: Later King of Qin Yao Chang led seventy thousand troops to attack Qin; King Fu Jian of Qin sent Yang Bi and others to oppose them and was defeated by Chang;
translations.idiomatic: Later King Yao Chang marched against Qin with seventy thousand men; Fu Jian sent Yang Bi and others to meet him and was defeated;

sentences.zh: 獲楊璧及右將軍徐成、鎮軍將軍毛盛等將吏數十人，萇皆禮而遣之。

translations.literal: he captured Yang Bi, Right General Xu Cheng, Guard-the-Army General Mao Sheng, and several tens of generals and officials; Chang treated them all with courtesy and sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: Chang captured Yang Bi, right general Xu Cheng, guard-the-army general Mao Sheng, and dozens of other officers—and sent them all back with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 燕慕容麟撥常山，秦苻亮、苻謨皆降。

translations.literal: Murong Lin of Yan swept Changshan; Qin's Fu Liang and Fu Mo both surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Lin overran Changshan; Fu Liang and Fu Mo of Qin surrendered.

sentences.zh: 麟進圍中山，秋，七月，克之，執苻鑒。

translations.literal: Lin advanced and besieged Zhongshan; in autumn, the seventh month, he captured it and seized Fu Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Lin pressed on to besiege Zhongshan; in autumn, during the seventh month, he took the city and captured Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 麟威聲大振，留屯中山。

translations.literal: Lin's prestige and renown greatly swelled, and he remained encamped at Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's fame spread far and wide, and he remained encamped at Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 秦幽州刺史王永、平州刺史苻沖帥二州之眾以擊燕。

translations.literal: Qin Governor of Youzhou Wang Yong and Governor of Pingzhou Fu Chong led the forces of the two provinces to attack Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yong, Qin's governor of Youzhou, and Fu Chong, governor of Pingzhou, led the armies of both provinces against Yan.

sentences.zh: 燕王垂遣寧朔將軍平規擊永，永遣昌黎太守宋敞逆戰於范陽，敞兵敗，規進據薊南。

translations.literal: King Murong Chui of Yan sent Pacifying-North General Ping Gui to attack Yong; Yong sent Administrator of Changli Song Chang to meet the attack at Fanyang; Chang's army was defeated, and Gui advanced and occupied the south of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: King Murong Chui sent Pacifying-North General Ping Gui against Yong; Yong dispatched Song Chang, administrator of Changli, to meet him at Fanyang, but Chang was defeated and Gui advanced to hold the south of Ji.

sentences.zh: 秦平原公暉帥洛陽、陝城之眾七萬歸於長安。

translations.literal: Qin Duke of Pingyuan Fu Hui led seventy thousand men of Luoyang and Shancheng back to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Hui, Duke of Pingyuan of Qin, led seventy thousand men from Luoyang and Shancheng back to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史王廣遣將軍王虯帥蜀漢之眾三萬北救長安。

translations.literal: Governor of Yizhou Wang Guang sent General Wang Jiu to lead thirty thousand men of Shu and Han north to relieve Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guang, governor of Yizhou, sent General Wang Jiu north with thirty thousand men from Shu and Han to relieve Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅聞慕容沖去長安浸近，乃引兵歸，遣撫軍大將軍高陽公方戍驪山，拜平原公暉為都督中外諸軍事、車騎大將軍、錄尚書事，配兵五萬以拒沖。

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin heard that Murong Chong was drawing gradually nearer to Chang'an, whereupon he led his army back, sent Pacifying-Army Grand General the Duke of Gaoyang Fang to garrison Lishan, appointed the Duke of Pingyuan Fu Hui as commander-in-chief of all armies at home and abroad, chariot-and-cavalry grand general, and recorder of the Masters of Writing affairs, and assigned him fifty thousand troops to oppose Chong.
translations.idiomatic: When King Fu Jian heard that Murong Chong was closing on Chang'an, he turned back with his army, posted Pacifying-Army Grand General Fang, Duke of Gaoyang, to garrison Lishan, and appointed Fu Hui, Duke of Pingyuan, commander-in-chief of all armies at home and abroad, chariot-and-cavalry grand general, and recorder of the Masters of Writing, giving him fifty thousand men to hold off Chong.

sentences.zh: 沖與暉戰於鄭西，大破之。

translations.literal: Chong fought Hui west of Zheng and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Chong met Hui west of Zheng and routed him completely.

sentences.zh: 堅又遣前將軍姜宇與少子河間公琳帥眾三萬拒沖於灞上；

translations.literal: Fu Jian again sent Forward General Jiang Yu and his younger son the Duke of Hejian Fu Lin to lead thirty thousand troops to oppose Chong at Bashang;
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian then sent Forward General Jiang Yu and his youngest son Fu Lin, Duke of Hejian, with thirty thousand men to block Chong at Bashang;

sentences.zh: 琳、宇皆敗死，沖遂據阿房城。

translations.literal: Lin and Yu were both defeated and killed, and Chong thereupon occupied Epang city.
translations.idiomatic: Lin and Yu were both defeated and killed, and Chong then seized Epang.

sentences.zh: 泰康回兵數敗，退還成都。

translations.literal: Kang Hui's returning army was repeatedly defeated and withdrew to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Hui's army, marching back, suffered repeated defeats and retreated to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 梓潼太守壘襲以涪城來降。

translations.literal: Administrator of Zitong Lei Xi came to surrender with Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Xi, administrator of Zitong, surrendered Fucheng to the invaders.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史桓石民據魯陽，遣河南太守高茂北戍洛陽。

translations.literal: Governor of Jingzhou Huan Shimin held Luyang and sent Administrator of Henan Gao Mao north to garrison Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Shimin, governor of Jingzhou, held Luyang and sent Gao Mao, administrator of Henan, north to garrison Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 己酉，葬康獻皇后於崇平陵。

translations.literal: On the day Jiyou, Empress Kangxian was buried at Chongping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiyou, Empress Kangxian was interred at Chongping Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 燕翟斌恃功驕縱，邀求無厭；

translations.literal: Zhai Bin of Yan relied on his merit and grew arrogant and unrestrained, making demands without end;
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Bin of Yan, swollen with his own merit, grew arrogant and insatiable in his demands;

sentences.zh: 又以鄴城久不下，潛有貳心。

translations.literal: moreover, because Ye had long failed to fall, he secretly harbored a divided heart.
translations.idiomatic: and because Ye still had not fallen after so long, he secretly began to waver in his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 太子寶請除之，燕王垂曰：「河南之盟，不可負也。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Bao asked that he be removed; King Murong Chui said: "The alliance of Henan must not be betrayed.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Murong Bao asked that Bin be eliminated, but King Murong Chui said, "The alliance we made at Henan must not be broken.

sentences.zh: 若其為難，罪由於斌。

translations.literal: If he makes trouble, the guilt will lie with Bin.
translations.idiomatic: If he turns against us, the fault will be his alone.

sentences.zh: 今事未有形而殺之，人必謂我忌憚其功能；

translations.literal: If we kill him now before anything has taken shape, men will surely say that we fear and envy his ability and merit;
translations.idiomatic: If we kill him now, before he has actually done wrong, men will say we fear his ability;

sentences.zh: 吾方收攬豪傑以隆大業，不可示人以狹，失天下之望也。

translations.literal: I am just now gathering heroes to exalt the great enterprise—I cannot show men a narrow mind and lose the hope of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: I am trying to gather heroes to raise up our great cause; I cannot show a petty spirit and lose the world's regard.

sentences.zh: 藉彼有謀，吾以智防之，無能為也。」

translations.literal: Even if he has designs, I shall guard against him with wisdom—he can do nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Even if he plots, I can outwit him; he will be powerless."

sentences.zh: 范陽王德、陳留王紹、驃騎大將軍農皆曰：「翟斌兄弟恃功而驕，必為國患。」

translations.literal: Prince of Fanyang Murong De, Prince of Chenliu Murong Shao, and Cavalry Grand General Murong Nong all said: "The brothers Zhai Bin rely on merit and are arrogant—they will surely become a calamity to the state."
translations.idiomatic: Murong De, Prince of Fanyang, Murong Shao, Prince of Chenliu, and Cavalry Grand General Murong Nong all said, "The Zhai brothers are arrogant with their merit; they will surely become a danger to the realm."

sentences.zh: 垂曰：「驕則速敗，焉能為患？

translations.literal: Chui said: "Arrogance brings swift ruin—how can it become a calamity?
translations.idiomatic: Chui replied, "Arrogance brings quick ruin—how could it become a lasting threat?

sentences.zh: 彼有大功，當聽其自斃耳。」

translations.literal: They have great merit; we should let them destroy themselves."
translations.idiomatic: They have done great service; let them destroy themselves in their own time."

sentences.zh: 禮遇彌重。

translations.literal: He treated them with courtesy more lavish than ever.
translations.idiomatic: And he honored Bin with even greater courtesy than before.

sentences.zh: 斌諷丁零及其黨請斌為尚書令。

translations.literal: Bin prompted the Dingling and his partisans to request that Bin be made Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Bin had the Dingling and his followers petition that he be made minister of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 垂曰：「翟王之功，宜居上輔；

translations.literal: Chui said: "Prince Zhai's merit properly qualifies him for the highest auxiliary post;
translations.idiomatic: Chui said, "Prince Zhai's merit would indeed suit the highest ministerial rank;

sentences.zh: 但台既未建，此官不可遽置耳。」

translations.literal: but since the imperial secretariat has not yet been established, this office cannot be set up at once."
translations.idiomatic: but the imperial secretariat has not yet been established, so the office cannot be created just yet."

sentences.zh: 斌努，密與前秦長樂公丕通謀，使丁零決堤潰水；

translations.literal: Bin grew angry, secretly entered into conspiracy with Former Qin Duke of Changle Fu Pi, and had the Dingling break the dikes and release the floodwaters;
translations.idiomatic: Bin, enraged, secretly plotted with Fu Pi, Duke of Changle of Qin, and had the Dingling break the dikes and flood the camp;

sentences.zh: 事覺，垂殺斌及其弟檀、敏，餘皆赦之。

translations.literal: when the affair was discovered, Chui killed Bin and his brothers Tan and Min, and pardoned all the rest.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was discovered, Chui executed Bin and his brothers Tan and Min and pardoned the rest.

sentences.zh: 斌兄子真，夜將營眾北奔邯鄲，引兵還向鄴圍，欲與丕內外相應。

translations.literal: Bin's nephew Zhen, by night led the camp troops north in flight to Handan, then turned his army back toward the siege of Ye, intending to coordinate with Pi inside and out.
translations.idiomatic: Bin's nephew Zhen fled north by night with the camp troops to Handan, then marched back against the siege of Ye, hoping to coordinate with Pi from within and without.

sentences.zh: 太子寶與冠軍大將軍隆擊破之，真還走邯鄲。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Bao and Champion Grand General Murong Long defeated him, and Zhen fled back to Handan.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Bao and Champion Grand General Murong Long routed him, and Zhen fled back to Handan.

sentences.zh: 太原王楷、陳留王紹言於垂曰：「丁零非有大志，但寵過為亂耳。

translations.literal: Prince of Taiyuan Murong Kai and Prince of Chenliu Murong Shao said to Chui: "The Dingling have no great ambition; they rebel only because favor has been carried too far.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Kai, Prince of Taiyuan, and Murong Shao, Prince of Chenliu, told Chui, "The Dingling have no grand ambitions; they turned to rebellion only because they were indulged too much.

sentences.zh: 今急之則屯聚為寇，緩之則自散。

translations.literal: If we press them now they will gather and become bandits; if we relax, they will disperse of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Press them hard and they will band together as raiders; leave them alone and they will scatter on their own.

sentences.zh: 散而擊之，無不克矣」垂從之。

translations.literal: Strike them once they scatter, and none will fail to be overcome." Chui followed this counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Strike them after they scatter, and you cannot fail." Chui agreed.

sentences.zh: 龜茲王帛純窘急，重賂獪胡以求救；

translations.literal: King Bo Chun of Kucha, hard pressed, heavily bribed the Kuaihu to seek rescue;
translations.idiomatic: King Bo Chun of Kucha, in desperate straits, lavished bribes on the Kuaihu to beg for relief;

sentences.zh: 獪胡王遣其弟吶龍、侯將馗帥騎二十餘萬，並引溫宿、尉頭等諸國兵合七十餘萬以救龜茲；

translations.literal: the king of the Kuaihu sent his younger brothers Nalong and Hou Jiangkui to lead more than two hundred thousand horsemen, and together with the troops of Wenxi, Weitou, and other states totaled more than seven hundred thousand to rescue Kucha;
translations.idiomatic: the Kuaihu king sent his younger brothers Nalong and Hou Jiangkui with more than two hundred thousand cavalry, and together with the armies of Wenxi, Weitou, and other states raised a force of more than seven hundred thousand to relieve Kucha;

sentences.zh: 秦呂光與戰於城西，大破之。

translations.literal: Lü Guang of Qin fought them west of the city and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang of Qin met them west of the city and crushed them completely.

sentences.zh: 帛純出走，王侯降者三十餘國。

translations.literal: Bo Chun fled; kings and lords who surrendered numbered more than thirty states.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Chun fled, and more than thirty kingdoms submitted.

sentences.zh: 光入其城，城如長安市邑，宮室甚盛。

translations.literal: Guang entered the city; its walls and wards were like those of Chang'an, and its palaces and halls were very grand.
translations.idiomatic: Guang entered the city and found its streets laid out like Chang'an's and its palaces magnificently built.

sentences.zh: 光撫寧西域，威恩甚著，遠方諸國，前世所不能服者，皆來歸附，上漢所賜節傳。

translations.literal: Guang pacified and settled the Western Regions; his authority and kindness were greatly manifest, and distant states that former ages had been unable to subdue all came to submit, presenting the tallies and credentials Han had bestowed upon them.
translations.idiomatic: Guang pacified the Western Regions with a reputation for both might and mercy; distant states that no previous dynasty had been able to subdue came to submit, surrendering the tallies and credentials Han had once granted them.

sentences.zh: 光皆表而易之，立帛純弟震為龜茲王。

translations.literal: Guang memorialized the throne and replaced them all, installing Bo Chun's younger brother Zhen as king of Kucha.
translations.idiomatic: Guang reported this to court and replaced all the credentials, installing Bo Chun's younger brother Zhen as king of Kucha.

sentences.zh: 八月，翟真自邯鄲北走，燕王垂遣太原王楷、驃騎大將軍農帥騎馬追之，甲寅，及於下邑。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Zhai Zhen fled north from Handan; King Murong Chui sent Prince of Taiyuan Murong Kai and Cavalry Grand General Murong Nong to pursue him with horse troops; on the day Jiayin they caught up with him at Xiayi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Zhai Zhen fled north from Handan; King Murong Chui sent Murong Kai, Prince of Taiyuan, and Cavalry Grand General Murong Nong in pursuit with cavalry, and on the day Jiayin they overtook him at Xiayi.

sentences.zh: 楷欲戰，農曰：「士卒饑倦，且視賊營不見丁壯，殆有他伏。」

translations.literal: Kai wished to give battle; Nong said: "The soldiers are hungry and weary, and when we look at the enemy camp we see no able-bodied men—there is probably another ambush."
translations.idiomatic: Kai wanted to fight, but Nong said, "Our men are hungry and exhausted, and the enemy camp shows no able-bodied troops—there is likely an ambush."

sentences.zh: 楷不從，進戰，燕兵大敗。

translations.literal: Kai would not listen, advanced to battle, and the Yan army suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Kai refused to listen, gave battle, and the Yan army was routed.

sentences.zh: 真北趨中山，屯於承營。

translations.literal: Zhen hurried north toward Zhongshan and encamped at Chengying.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen pressed north toward Zhongshan and encamped at Chengying.

sentences.zh: 鄴中芻糧俱盡，削松木以飼馬。

translations.literal: In Ye, fodder and grain were entirely exhausted, and pine wood was shaved to feed the horses.
translations.idiomatic: Inside Ye, fodder and grain were completely exhausted, and they shaved pine bark to feed the horses.

sentences.zh: 燕王垂謂諸將曰：「苻丕窮寇，必無降理，不如退屯新城，開丕西歸之路，以謝秦王疇昔之恩，且為討翟真之計。」

translations.literal: King Murong Chui said to his generals: "Fu Pi is a cornered foe and will surely not surrender; it would be better to withdraw and encamp at Xincheng, open a path west for Pi to return, thereby repaying King Fu Jian's former kindness, and also make plans to attack Zhai Zhen."
translations.idiomatic: King Murong Chui told his generals, "Fu Pi is a desperate enemy and will never surrender. Better to withdraw to Xincheng and leave him a road west, repaying King Fu Jian's old kindness and freeing us to deal with Zhai Zhen."

sentences.zh: 丙寅夜，垂解圍趨新城。

translations.literal: On the night of the day Bingyin, Chui lifted the siege and hastened to Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: That night, on the day Bingyin, Chui raised the siege and marched for Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 遣慕容農徇清河、平原，征督租賦，農明立約束，均適有無，軍令嚴整，無所侵暴，由是谷帛屬路，軍資豐給。

translations.literal: He sent Murong Nong to sweep Qinghe and Pingyuan, collecting and supervising taxes and levies; Nong clearly established regulations, equalizing what was had and lacked, and military orders were strict and orderly with no plundering—whereupon grain and cloth lined the roads and military supplies were abundantly furnished.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Murong Nong through Qinghe and Pingyuan to collect taxes and levies; Nong set clear rules, sharing out supplies fairly, kept discipline strict, and forbade all pillage, so grain and cloth lined the roads and the army was abundantly supplied.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，南昌文穆公郗愔薨。

translations.literal: On the day Wuyin, Xi Yin, Duke of Nanchang and posthumously titled Wennu, died.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Wuyin, Xi Yin, Duke of Nanchang posthumously styled Wennu, died.

sentences.zh: 太保安奏請乘苻氏傾敗，開拓中原，以徐、兗二州刺史謝玄為前鋒都督，帥豫州刺史桓石虔等伐秦。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Xie An memorialized asking to take advantage of the Fu clan's collapse to open up the Central Plains, appointing Xie Xuan, governor of Xu and Yan provinces, as vanguard commander-in-chief, and leading Governor of Yuzhou Huan Shiqian and others to attack Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Xie An memorialized the throne, urging that Jin seize the moment of the Fu clan's collapse to recover the Central Plains; Xie Xuan, governor of Xu and Yan, was made vanguard commander-in-chief, and with Huan Shiqian, governor of Yuzhou, and others he marched against Qin.

sentences.zh: 玄至下邳，秦徐州刺史趙遷棄彭城走，充進據彭城。

translations.literal: Xuan reached Xiapi; Qin Governor of Xuzhou Zhao Qian abandoned Pengcheng and fled, and Xuan advanced and occupied Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan reached Xiapi; Zhao Qian, Qin's governor of Xuzhou, abandoned Pengcheng and fled, and Xuan advanced to take the city.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅聞呂光平西域，以光為都督玉門以西諸軍事、西域校尉；

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin heard that Lü Guang had pacified the Western Regions and appointed Guang commander-in-chief of all armies west of Yumen and colonel of the Western Regions;
translations.idiomatic: When King Fu Jian heard that Lü Guang had pacified the Western Regions, he appointed Guang commander-in-chief of all armies west of Yumen and colonel of the Western Regions;

sentences.zh: 道絕，不通。

translations.literal: the road was cut off and no communication was possible.
translations.idiomatic: but the road was cut and no word could get through.

sentences.zh: 秦幽州刺史王永求救於振威將軍劉庫仁，庫仁遣其妻兄公孫希帥騎三千救之，大破平規於薊南，乘勝長驅，進據唐城，與慕容麟相持。

translations.literal: Qin Governor of Youzhou Wang Yong sought rescue from Quelling-Authority General Liu Kuren; Kuren sent his wife's elder brother Gongsun Xi to lead three thousand horsemen to relieve him; Xi routed Ping Gui south of Ji, drove forward on the momentum of victory, advanced and occupied Tangcheng, and faced Murong Lin in stalemate.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yong, Qin's governor of Youzhou, appealed to Quelling-Authority General Liu Kuren for help; Kuren sent his brother-in-law Gongsun Xi with three thousand cavalry, who routed Ping Gui south of Ji, pressed the victory, seized Tangcheng, and locked in stalemate with Murong Lin.

sentences.zh: 九月，謝玄使彭城內史劉牢之攻秦兗州刺史張崇。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Xie Xuan sent Administrator of Pengcheng Liu Laozhi to attack Qin Governor of Yanzhou Zhang Chong.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Xie Xuan sent Liu Laozhi, administrator of Pengcheng, against Zhang Chong, Qin's governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，崇棄鄄城奔燕。

translations.literal: On the day Xinmao, Chong abandoned Juancheng and fled to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Xinmao, Zhang Chong abandoned Juancheng and fled to Yan.

sentences.zh: 寧之據鄄城，河南城堡皆來歸附。

translations.literal: Laozhi occupied Juancheng, and all the fortified places of Henan came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi took Juancheng, and fortified posts throughout Henan submitted to Jin.

sentences.zh: 太保安上疏自求北征。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Xie An submitted a memorial asking to lead the northern campaign himself.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Xie An memorialized the throne, asking to lead the northern campaign in person.

sentences.zh: 甲午，加安都督揚、江等十五州諸軍事，加黃鉞。

translations.literal: On the day Jiawu, An was additionally made commander-in-chief of the armies of Yang, Jiang, and fourteen other provinces, and given the yellow battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiawu, An was further appointed commander-in-chief over fifteen provinces including Yang and Jiang, and granted the yellow battle-axe.

sentences.zh: 慕容沖進逼長安，秦王堅登城觀之，歎曰：「此虜何從出哉！」

translations.literal: Murong Chong pressed close upon Chang'an; King Fu Jian of Qin mounted the wall to look at him and sighed: "Where did this bandit come from!"
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chong closed in on Chang'an; King Fu Jian mounted the wall to look out and sighed, "Where did this foe come from!"

sentences.zh: 大呼責沖曰：「奴何苦來送死！」

translations.literal: He shouted loudly and rebuked Chong: "Slave, why have you come so far only to seek death!"
translations.idiomatic: He shouted down at Chong, "You slave—why come all this way just to die!"

sentences.zh: 沖曰：「奴厭奴苦，欲取汝為代耳！」

translations.literal: Chong said: "The slave is weary of the slave's suffering and wishes to take your place!"
translations.idiomatic: Chong answered, "Your slave is sick of servitude and means to take your place!

sentences.zh: 沖少有寵於堅，堅遣使以錦袍稱詔遺之。

translations.literal: Chong had once enjoyed favor with Fu Jian; Fu Jian sent an envoy with an imperial edict conveyed by a brocade robe as a gift to him.
translations.idiomatic: Chong had once been a favorite of Fu Jian's; Fu Jian now sent an envoy bearing a brocade robe with a message styled as an imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 沖遺詹事稱皇太弟令答之曰：「孤今心在天下，豈顧一袍小惠！

translations.literal: Chong sent his household steward with a reply styled as an imperial younger brother-heir's order, saying: "I now set my heart on the realm—how should I care for the small favor of one robe!
translations.idiomatic: Chong replied through his household steward in the name of the imperial younger brother-heir: "My heart is set on the realm—why should I care for the petty gift of a robe!

sentences.zh: 苟能知命，君臣束手，早送皇帝！

translations.literal: If you can know fate, let ruler and ministers bind their hands and send the emperor out early!
translations.idiomatic: If you know what fate demands, let ruler and ministers surrender and deliver the emperor at once!

sentences.zh: 自當寬貸苻氏，以酬曩好。」

translations.literal: Of myself I shall show leniency to the Fu clan, to repay our former friendship."
translations.idiomatic: I will then show mercy to the Fu clan, in repayment of our old affection."

sentences.zh: 堅大怒曰：「吾不用王景略、陽平公之言，使白虜敢至於此！」

translations.literal: Fu Jian grew greatly angry and said: "Because I did not heed the words of Wang Jinglue and the Duke of Yangping, these white barbarians dare come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian flew into a rage and cried, "Had I heeded Wang Meng and the Duke of Yangping, these white barbarians would never have dared come so far!"

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛亥朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the new-moon day Xinghai, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, during the tenth month, on the new moon of the day Xinghai, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，大赦。

translations.literal: On the day Yichou, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Yichou, the court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 謝玄遣陰陵太守高素攻秦青州刺史苻郎，軍至琅邪，朗來降。

translations.literal: Xie Xuan sent Administrator of Yinling Gao Su to attack Qin Governor of Qingzhou Fu Lang; when the army reached Langye, Lang came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xuan sent Gao Su, administrator of Yinling, against Fu Lang, Qin's governor of Qingzhou; when the army reached Langye, Lang surrendered.

sentences.zh: 朗，堅之從子也。

translations.literal: Lang was Fu Jian's younger cousin's son.
translations.idiomatic: Lang was Fu Jian's cousin's son.

sentences.zh: 翟真在承營，與公孫希、宋敞遙相首尾。

translations.literal: Zhai Zhen was at Chengying, coordinating from afar with Gongsun Xi and Song Chang in mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Zhen held Chengying, coordinating at a distance with Gongsun Xi and Song Chang in mutual support.

sentences.zh: 長樂公丕遣宦者冗從僕射清河光祚，將兵數百赴中山，與真相結。

translations.literal: Duke of Changle Fu Pi sent the eunuch attendant-extras servant-director Guang Zuo of Qinghe, leading several hundred troops to go to Zhongshan and join forces with Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi, Duke of Changle, sent the eunuch attendant Guang Zuo of Qinghe with several hundred troops to Zhongshan to ally with Zhen.

sentences.zh: 又遣陽平太守邵興將數千騎，招集冀州故郡縣，與祚期會襄國。

translations.literal: He also sent Administrator of Yangping Shao Xing to lead several thousand horsemen to summon the former commanderies and counties of Jizhou, arranging to meet Guang Zuo at Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Shao Xing, administrator of Yangping, with several thousand cavalry to rally the old commanderies and counties of Jizhou, arranging to rendezvous with Guang Zuo at Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 是時，燕軍疲弊，秦勢復振，冀州郡縣皆觀望成敗，趙郡人趙粟等起兵柏鄉以應興。

translations.literal: At this time the Yan army was worn and exhausted while Qin's strength revived; commanderies and counties of Jizhou all watched to see which side would prevail, and Zhao Su of Zhao commandery and others raised troops at Baixiang to respond to Shao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Yan army was exhausted while Qin was rallying again; commanderies and counties across Jizhou waited to see which side would win, and Zhao Su of Zhao commandery and others rose at Baixiang in support of Shao Xing.

sentences.zh: 燕王垂遣冠軍大將軍隆、龍驤將軍張崇將兵邀擊興，命驃騎大將軍農自清河引兵會之。

translations.literal: King Murong Chui sent Champion Grand General Murong Long and Soaring-Dragon General Zhang Chong to lead troops and intercept Shao Xing, ordering Cavalry Grand General Murong Nong to lead troops from Qinghe to join them.
translations.idiomatic: King Murong Chui sent Champion Grand General Murong Long and Soaring-Dragon General Zhang Chong to intercept Shao Xing, and ordered Cavalry Grand General Murong Nong to march from Qinghe to join them.

sentences.zh: 隆與興戰於襄國，大破之；

translations.literal: Long fought Shao Xing at Xiangguo and routed him utterly;
translations.idiomatic: Long met Shao Xing at Xiangguo and routed him;

sentences.zh: 興走至廣阿，遇慕容農，執之。

translations.literal: Shao Xing fled to Guanga and encountered Murong Nong, who seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Xing fled to Guanga, ran into Murong Nong, and was captured.

sentences.zh: 光祚聞之，循西山走歸鄴。

translations.literal: Guang Zuo heard of this and fled along the western hills back to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: When Guang Zuo heard the news, he fled along the western hills back to Ye.

sentences.zh: 隆遂擊趙粟等，皆破之，冀州郡縣復從燕。

translations.literal: Long then attacked Zhao Su and the others, defeating them all, and the commanderies and counties of Jizhou again followed Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Long then defeated Zhao Su and the others, and the commanderies and counties of Jizhou submitted to Yan once more.

sentences.zh: 劉庫仁聞公孫希已破平規，欲大舉兵以救長樂公丕，發雁門、上谷、代郡兵，屯繁畤。

translations.literal: Liu Kuren heard that Gongsun Xi had already defeated Ping Gui and wished to raise a great army to rescue Duke of Changle Fu Pi; he mobilized the troops of Yanmen, Shanggu, and Dai commanderies and encamped at Fanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Kuren heard that Gongsun Xi had already defeated Ping Gui, he planned a major relief expedition for Fu Pi, Duke of Changle, mustering troops from Yanmen, Shanggu, and Dai and encamping at Fanzhi.

sentences.zh: 燕太子太保輿句之子文、零陵公慕輿虔之子常時在庫仁所，知三郡兵不樂遠所，因作亂，夜，攻庫仁，殺之，竊其駿馬奔燕。

translations.literal: Wen, son of Yuju, grand preceptor of the Yan crown prince, and Chang, son of Murong Qian, Duke of Lingling, were then with Kuren; knowing that the troops of the three commanderies were unwilling to go far from home, they therefore raised a revolt; by night they attacked Kuren, killed him, stole his fine horses, and fled to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Wen, son of Yuju, grand preceptor to the Yan crown prince, and Chang, son of Murong Qian, Duke of Lingling, were then in Kuren's camp; knowing the three commanderies' troops had no stomach for a distant campaign, they mutinied by night, killed Kuren, seized his best horses, and fled to Yan.

sentences.zh: 公孫希之眾聞亂自潰，希奔翟真。

translations.literal: Gongsun Xi's troops, hearing of the turmoil, dispersed of themselves; Xi fled to Zhai Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Xi's army, hearing of the revolt, broke apart on its own; Xi fled to Zhai Zhen.

sentences.zh: 庫仁弟頭眷代領庫仁部眾。

translations.literal: Kuren's younger brother Tou Juan took over command of Kuren's troops in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Kuren's younger brother Tou Juan took command of his brother's forces.

sentences.zh: 秦長樂公丕遣光祚及參軍封孚召驃騎將軍張蚝、并州刺史王騰於晉陽以自救，蚝、騰以眾少不能赴。

translations.literal: Fu Pi, Duke of Changle of Qin, sent Guang Zuo and staff officer Feng Fu to summon Cavalry General Zhang Hao and Governor of Bingzhou Wang Teng at Jinyang to save himself; Hao and Teng, finding their forces too few, could not come.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi, Duke of Changle of Qin, sent Guang Zuo and staff officer Feng Fu to summon Cavalry General Zhang Hao and Wang Teng, governor of Bingzhou, at Jinyang to his aid; but Hao and Teng, with too few men, could not come.

sentences.zh: 丕進退路窮，謀於僚佐。

translations.literal: Pi, advancing and retreating, found his paths exhausted and consulted his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Pi, with advance blocked and retreat cut off, consulted his advisers.

sentences.zh: 司馬楊膺請自歸於晉，丕未許。

translations.literal: Chief administrator Yang Ying asked to surrender to Jin of his own accord; Pi did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Chief administrator Yang Ying proposed surrendering to Jin; Pi refused.

sentences.zh: 會謝玄遣龍驤將軍劉牢之等據碻磝，濟陽太守郭滿據滑台，將軍顏肱、劉襲軍於河北；

translations.literal: It happened that Xie Xuan sent Soaring-Dragon General Liu Laozhi and others to occupy Qiao'ao, Administrator of Jiyang Guo Man to hold Huatai, and Generals Yan Gong and Liu Xi to encamp north of the Yellow River;
translations.idiomatic: Just then Xie Xuan sent Soaring-Dragon General Liu Laozhi and others to hold Qiao'ao, Guo Man, administrator of Jiyang, to hold Huatai, and Generals Yan Gong and Liu Xi to camp north of the Yellow River;

sentences.zh: 丕遣將軍桑據屯黎陽以據之。

translations.literal: Pi sent General Sang Ju to encamp at Liyang and hold them off.
translations.idiomatic: Pi sent General Sang Ju to garrison Liyang and block them.

sentences.zh: 劉襲夜襲據，走之，遂克黎陽。

translations.literal: Liu Xi attacked Sang Ju by night, drove him off, and thereupon captured Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xi raided Sang Ju by night, drove him off, and took Liyang.

sentences.zh: 丕懼，乃遣從弟就與參軍焦逵請救於玄，致書稱「欲假途求糧，西赴國難，須援軍既接，以鄴與之。
