translations.literal: Pi, in fear, thereupon sent his younger cousin Jiu and staff officer Jiao Kui to beg rescue from Xie Xuan, sending a letter stating: "I wish to borrow a road to seek grain and march west to meet the state's crisis; once relief troops have joined me, I will give Ye to you.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Pi sent his cousin Jiu and staff officer Jiao Kui to beg aid from Xie Xuan with a letter saying, "I wish to pass through your lines to gather grain and march west to the empire's defense; once your relief force joins me, I will hand over Ye.

sentences.zh: 若西路不通，長安陷沒，請帥所領保守鄴城。」

translations.literal: If the western road is blocked and Chang'an falls, I ask to lead my command and hold Ye."
translations.idiomatic: If the road west is cut and Chang'an falls, I ask only to hold Ye with the forces under my command."

sentences.zh: 逵與參軍姜讓密謂楊膺曰：「今喪敗如此，長安阻絕，存亡不可知。

translations.literal: Jiao Kui and staff officer Jiang Rang secretly said to Yang Ying: "Now defeat is so complete, Chang'an is cut off, and survival or destruction cannot be known.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Kui and staff officer Jiang Rang secretly told Yang Ying, "We are beaten this badly, Chang'an is cut off, and no one knows whether the dynasty will survive.

sentences.zh: 屈節竭誠以求糧援，猶懼不獲；

translations.literal: Even if we humble ourselves and exhaust our sincerity to seek grain and relief, we still fear we may not obtain it;
translations.idiomatic: Even if we humbly and faithfully beg for grain and aid, we may still fail;

sentences.zh: 而公豪氣不除，方設兩端，事必無成。

translations.literal: yet you, sir, have not put aside your proud spirit and are still setting up two paths—the affair will surely fail.
translations.idiomatic: yet you still cling to your pride and hedge between two courses—the mission is doomed.

sentences.zh: 宜正書為表，許以王師之至，當致身南歸；

translations.literal: You ought to draw up a proper letter as a memorial, promising that when the royal army arrives you will give yourself over and return south;
translations.idiomatic: You should write a proper memorial promising that when the imperial army arrives you will surrender and return south;

sentences.zh: 如其不從，可逼縛與之。」

translations.literal: if he will not comply, you can force and bind him and hand him over."
translations.idiomatic: and if he refuses, bind him by force and deliver him up.

sentences.zh: 膺自以力能制丕，乃改書而遣之。

translations.literal: Ying, believing himself able to control Pi, thereupon revised the letter and sent it off.
translations.idiomatic: Ying, confident he could control Pi, rewrote the letter accordingly and dispatched it.

sentences.zh: 謝玄遣晉陵太守滕恬之渡河守黎陽。

translations.literal: Xie Xuan sent Administrator of Jinling Teng Tianzhi to cross the river and hold Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xuan sent Teng Tianzhi, administrator of Jinling, across the river to garrison Liyang.

sentences.zh: 恬之，修之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Tianzhi was the great-grandson of Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzhi was the great-grandson of Teng Xiu.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以兗、青、司、豫既平，加玄都督徐、兗、青、司、冀、幽、并七州諸軍事。

translations.literal: The court, because Yan, Qing, Si, and Yu had already been pacified, promoted Xie Xuan to commander-in-chief of military affairs for the seven provinces Xu, Yan, Qing, Si, Ji, You, and Bing.
translations.idiomatic: With Yan, Qing, Si, and Yu now pacified, the court promoted Xie Xuan to overall commander of military affairs in Xu, Yan, Qing, Si, Ji, You, and Bing—seven provinces in all.

sentences.zh: 後秦王萇聞慕容沖攻長安，會群僚議進止，皆曰：「大王宜先取長安，建立根本，然後經營四方。」

translations.literal: Later King of Qin Yao Chang heard that Murong Chong was attacking Chang'an; he convened his officials to discuss advancing or holding back, and all said: "Your Majesty ought first to take Chang'an and establish a foundation, and then manage the four quarters."
translations.idiomatic: Later King Yao Chang heard that Murong Chong was besieging Chang'an and gathered his ministers to debate their course. All agreed: "Your Majesty should seize Chang'an first, secure a base, and only then turn to the four quarters."

sentences.zh: 萇曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Chang said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Chang replied, "No.

sentences.zh: 燕人因其眾有思歸之心以起兵，若得其志，必不久留關中。

translations.literal: The Yan men raised troops because their masses harbored a desire to return home; if they obtain their aim, they will surely not long remain in Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan rebels rose because their followers long to go home; once they get what they want, they will not stay in Guanzhong for long.

sentences.zh: 吾當移屯嶺北，廣收資實，以待秦亡燕去，然後拱手取之耳。」

translations.literal: I ought to shift camp north of the ridges, broadly gather resources and strength, and wait until Qin perishes and Yan departs—then I shall take it with folded hands, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: I should move north of the ridges, gather stores and strength, and wait until Qin collapses and the Yan leave—then I can take the prize without lifting a finger."

sentences.zh: 乃留其長子興守北地，使寧北將軍姚穆守同官川，自將其眾攻新平。

translations.literal: Thereupon he left his eldest son Xing to hold Beidi, made Pacify-North General Yao Mu hold Tongguan River, and personally led his force to attack Xinping.
translations.idiomatic: He left his eldest son Xing to hold Beidi, posted Pacify-North General Yao Mu on the Tongguan River, and marched in person against Xinping.

sentences.zh: 初，新平人殺其郡將，秦王堅缺其城角以恥之，新平民望深以為病，欲立忠義以雪之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the people of Xinping killed their commandery general; King Fu Jian of Qin had a corner of the city wall cut away to shame them—the prominent men of Xinping felt this deeply as a disgrace and wished to establish righteousness to wipe it away.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the people of Xinping had killed their commandery commander; King Fu Jian had a corner of the city wall cut away to humiliate them. Xinping's leading men took this as a deep disgrace and yearned to prove their loyalty and redeem the shame.

sentences.zh: 及後秦王萇至新平，新平太守南安苟輔欲降之，郡人遼西太守馮傑、蓮勺令馮羽、尚書郎趙義、汶山太守馮苗諫曰：「昔田單以一城存齊。

translations.literal: When Later King of Qin Yao Chang reached Xinping, Administrator of Xinping Gou Fu of Nan'an wished to surrender to him; men of the commandery—Administrator of Liaoxi Feng Jie, Magistrate of Lianqiao Feng Yu, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing Zhao Yi, and Administrator of Wenshan Feng Miao—remonstrated, saying: "In antiquity Tian Dan preserved Qi with a single city.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Chang reached Xinping, Gou Fu, administrator of Xinping, wanted to surrender. Feng Jie of Liaoxi, Feng Yu of Lianqiao, Zhao Yi of the Masters of Writing, and Feng Miao of Wenshan remonstrated with him: "Long ago Tian Dan saved Qi from a single city.

sentences.zh: 今秦之州鎮，猶連城過百，奈何遽為叛臣乎！」

translations.literal: Now Qin's prefectures and garrisons still link in more than a hundred cities—how can we so quickly become rebellious ministers!"
translations.idiomatic: Qin still holds more than a hundred linked cities and garrisons—how can we so readily play the traitor!"

sentences.zh: 輔喜曰：「此吾志也，但恐久而無救，郡人橫被無辜。

translations.literal: Fu gladly said: "This is my wish, but I fear that if help is slow in coming, the people of the commandery will suffer innocent harm.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was delighted. "That is my own wish—but I fear that if relief does not come soon, the people will suffer without cause.

sentences.zh: 諸君能爾，吾豈顧生哉！」

translations.literal: If you gentlemen can act thus, how would I care for my own life!"
translations.idiomatic: If you gentlemen are willing to do this, what is my life to me!"

sentences.zh: 於是憑城固守。

translations.literal: Thereupon they leaned on the city and held fast.
translations.idiomatic: They then held the city in a determined defense.

sentences.zh: 後秦為土山地道，輔亦於內為之，或戰地下，或戰山上，後秦眾死者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Later Qin built ramparts of earth and underground tunnels; Fu likewise built them within; sometimes they fought underground, sometimes on the hills—Later Qin troops who died numbered more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qin raised earthworks and dug tunnels; Fu matched them from inside. Battles raged underground and on the heights alike, and Later Qin lost more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 輔詐降以誘萇，萇將入城，覺之而返；

translations.literal: Fu feigned surrender to lure Chang; Chang was about to enter the city, detected the ruse, and turned back;
translations.idiomatic: Fu feigned surrender to lure Chang in; Chang was on the point of entering the city when he saw through the trick and withdrew;

sentences.zh: 輔仗兵邀擊，幾獲之，又殺萬餘人。

translations.literal: Fu relied on arms to intercept and strike, almost capturing him, and killed more than ten thousand men again.
translations.idiomatic: Fu ambushed him with troops and nearly took him, killing another ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 隴西處士王嘉，隱居倒虎山，有異術，能知未然，秦人神之。

translations.literal: Wang Jia, a reclusive scholar of Longxi, lived in seclusion on Mount Daohu; he had unusual arts and could know what had not yet come to pass—the people of Qin regarded him as divine.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jia, a recluse of Longxi, lived in seclusion on Mount Daohu. He possessed uncanny powers and could foresee events yet to come; the people of Qin revered him as a sage.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅、後秦王萇及慕容沖皆遣使迎之。

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin, Later King of Qin Yao Chang, and Murong Chong all sent envoys to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian, Later King Yao Chang, and Murong Chong all sent envoys to fetch him.

sentences.zh: 十一月，嘉入長安，眾聞之，以為堅有福，故聖人助之，三輔堡壁及四山氐、羌歸堅者四萬餘人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Jia entered Chang'an; when the masses heard of it, they thought Fu Jian was blessed and that a sage therefore aided him—fortified strongholds of the Three Adjuncts and Di and Qiang of the four mountains who returned to Fu Jian numbered more than forty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Jia entered Chang'an. People took it as a sign that Fu Jian enjoyed Heaven's favor—a sage had come to his aid—and more than forty thousand men from the fortified camps of the Three Adjuncts and from the Di and Qiang of the surrounding hills rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 堅置嘉及沙門道安於外殿，動靜咨之。

translations.literal: Fu Jian installed Jia and the monk Dao An in the outer hall and consulted them on every move.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian quartered Jia and the monk Dao An in the outer hall and consulted them on every decision.

sentences.zh: 燕慕容農自信都西擊丁零翟遼於魯口，破之。

translations.literal: Murong Nong of Yan from west of Xindu attacked the Dingling Zhai Liao at Lukou and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Nong marched west from Xindu, struck the Dingling chieftain Zhai Liao at Lukou, and routed him.

sentences.zh: 遼退屯無極，農屯蒿城以逼之。

translations.literal: Liao withdrew and encamped at Wuji; Nong encamped at Haocheng to press him.
translations.idiomatic: Liao fell back to Wuji while Nong camped at Haocheng to hem him in.

sentences.zh: 遼，真之從兄也。

translations.literal: Liao was the elder cousin of Zhen on the father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Liao was Zhai Zhen's elder cousin.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑在長安城中者猶千餘人，慕容紹之兄肅，與慕容□陰謀結鮮卑為亂。

translations.literal: Xianbei still in Chang'an numbered more than a thousand; Su, elder brother of Murong Shao, plotted secretly with Murong Wei (□ in source) to unite the Xianbei in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand Xianbei remained in Chang'an. Murong Su, Murong Shao's elder brother, plotted secretly with Murong Wei to rally the Xianbei in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 十二月，□白堅，以其子新昏，請堅幸其家，置酒，欲伏兵殺之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Wei told Fu Jian that because his son had newly wed, he asked Fu Jian to favor his home with a visit, set out wine, and intended to lay hidden troops to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Murong Wei told Fu Jian that his son had just married and invited Fu Jian to visit his home for a feast, planning to kill him with hidden troops.

sentences.zh: 堅許之，會天大雨，不果往。

translations.literal: Fu Jian consented; it happened that Heaven sent down great rain, and he did not go in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian agreed, but a torrential rainstorm intervened and he never went.

sentences.zh: 事覺，堅召□及肅，肅曰：「事必洩矣，入則俱死。

translations.literal: When the affair was discovered, Fu Jian summoned Wei and Su; Su said: "The matter has surely leaked; if we enter, we both die.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was discovered, Fu Jian summoned Murong Wei and Murong Su. Su said, "The secret is out—if we go in, we die together.

sentences.zh: 今城內已嚴，不如殺使者馳出，既得出門，大眾便集。

translations.literal: Now within the city defenses are already strict; better to kill the envoy and gallop out—once we have passed the gate, the great host will assemble at once.
translations.idiomatic: The city is already on alert—we should kill the messenger and ride out at full speed. Once we are through the gate, the rest will rally to us.

sentences.zh: □不從，遂俱入。

translations.literal: Wei did not follow; thereupon both entered together.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Wei refused; they went in together anyway.

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「吾相待何如，而起此意」？

translations.literal: Fu Jian said: "How have I treated you, that you should harbor such a design"?
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian asked, "After all I have done for you, why would you plot this?"

sentences.zh: □飾辭以對。

translations.literal: Wei adorned his words in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Wei answered with evasions.

sentences.zh: 肅曰：「家國事重，何論意氣！」

translations.literal: Su said: "Affairs of house and state are weighty—what room is there to speak of personal feeling!"
translations.idiomatic: Su cried, "The realm comes before any personal debt—what does gratitude matter now!"

sentences.zh: 堅先殺肅，乃殺□及其宗族，城內鮮卑無少長、男女，皆殺之。

translations.literal: Fu Jian first killed Su, then killed Wei and his clan; among the Xianbei within the city, whether young or old, male or female, all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian killed Su first, then Murong Wei and his entire clan. Every Xianbei in the city—young or old, man or woman—was put to the sword.

sentences.zh: 燕王垂幼子柔，養於宦者宋牙家為牙子，故得不坐，與太子寶之子盛乘間得出，奔慕容沖。

translations.literal: Murong Chui's youngest son by the Prince of Yan, Rou, was raised in eunuch Song Ya's household as his ward; therefore he was not implicated. With Sheng, son of Crown Prince Bao, he took advantage of an opening to get out and fled to Murong Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Rou, Murong Chui's youngest son, had been raised as a ward in the eunuch Song Ya's household and so escaped punishment. He and Sheng, son of Crown Prince Bao, slipped out in the confusion and fled to Murong Chong.

sentences.zh: 燕慕容麟、慕容農合兵襲翟遼，大破之，遼單騎奔翟真。

translations.literal: Murong Lin and Murong Nong of Yan combined forces and struck Zhai Liao, routing him greatly; Liao fled alone on horseback to Zhai Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Lin and Murong Nong combined their forces, smashed Zhai Liao, and drove him off; Liao fled alone to join Zhai Zhen.

sentences.zh: 燕王垂以秦長樂公丕猶據鄴不去，乃更引兵圍鄴，開其西走之路。

translations.literal: Murong Chui, Prince of Yan, because Fu Pi, Duke of Changle of Qin, still held Ye and would not leave, thereupon again led troops to besiege Ye and opened a road for him to flee west.
translations.idiomatic: Because Fu Pi still held Ye and would not budge, Murong Chui returned to besiege the city, leaving the western road open for his escape.

sentences.zh: 焦逵見謝玄，玄欲征丕任子，然後出兵；

translations.literal: Jiao Kui saw Xie Xuan; Xie Xuan wished to take Fu Pi's hostage sons before sending out troops;
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Kui met with Xie Xuan, who wanted Fu Pi's sons held as hostages before he would march;

sentences.zh: 逵固陳丕款誠，並述楊膺之意，玄乃遣劉牢之、滕恬之等帥眾二萬救鄴。

translations.literal: Kui firmly set forth Pi's earnest sincerity and also explained Yang Ying's intent; Xie Xuan thereupon sent Liu Laozhi, Teng Tianzhi, and others to lead a force of twenty thousand to relieve Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Kui earnestly vouched for Pi's good faith and conveyed Yang Ying's message; Xie Xuan then sent Liu Laozhi, Teng Tianzhi, and others with twenty thousand men to relieve Ye.

sentences.zh: 丕告饑，玄水陸運米二千斛以饋之。

translations.literal: Pi reported famine; Xie Xuan transported two thousand hu of rice by land and water to supply him.
translations.idiomatic: When Pi reported famine, Xie Xuan shipped two thousand hu of grain to him by land and water.

sentences.zh: 秦梁州刺史潘猛棄漢中，奔長安。

translations.literal: Qin Governor of Liangzhou Pan Meng abandoned Hanzhong and fled to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Meng, Qin's governor of Liangzhou, abandoned Hanzhong and fled to Chang'an.
